DT6LqAHkgzS.content:
We went to banff for our honeymoon 2 weeks ago. It was the best time! We both aren't super outdoorsy, especially in the winter, so instead of the usual site seeing, we wanted to really experience what the town of Banff had to offer.

We scoped out some of the best food spots, indulged in some fun drinks and did a few classic touristy things. We also picked out a hotel we would want to spend a little bit of time at. One thing I noticed was EVERYONE was so friendly. From the hotel staff, cab drivers, servers, ect. Everyone we encountered or served us in banff added to our experience just by the way they treated us.

The Douglas Fir was affordable, quirky in its own ways, the rooms have full kitchenettes and fireplaces for you to use. This hotel is super kid friendly with a water slide, indoor hot tub and play place. Our favourite was the outdoor hot tub that had a mountain view. It was so lovely.

Our first day we happened to get beautiful views at every place we dined at! I would 10/10 eat at @melissas.missteak again. We didn't eat a full meal at The Waldhaus but it was a very unique place and the drinks are super tasty!

If you wanna see our dinner experience at the top of the @banffgondola I highly recommend you watch for part 2! Also, this video is not sponsored, I just love documenting our adventures and sharing them with you guys.

DT-o00wEahD.content:
A little recap: 2 weeks ago we went to Banff for our honeymoon! We stayed at the Douglas Fir Resort and had the best time taking in what the town of Banff has to offer, without spending a ton of time outdoors! 

My favourite experience on the whole trip, was our time at @banffgondola Even though I am terrified of heights, the views are absolutely amazing. The staff from the bottom, to the top and back were so friendly and accommodating. Plus, the sunset dining experience at @skybistrobanff and night time ride back down was very romantic 🥰❤️ 10/10 recommend.

We asked a lot of the locals what their go-to spots were for a Saturday Night. We kept hearing about a lot of the same places; Rose & Crown, Tommy's Neighborhood Pub, Melissa's Misssteak, High Rollers (we never made it to this one) and St. Jame's Gate Irish Pub. Our favourite was Tommy's, although it was so busy, the staff were welcoming, they had the cheapest drinks in banff and it was a vibe for anyone in their 20's and 30's. We even went back the next night for the cheap but tasty drinks!

The Juniper Bistro, is just outside of Banff, located inside the @juniperbanff They have a nature inspired, in-season, farm-to-plate feel to their menu. I got the benny flight, because its not every day I find a restaurant that actually has 3 different vegetarian eggs benedicts to try. They also had beautiful views to enjoy with your meal.

I'm sure your starting to see a trend now, we ate a lot of food 🤣 I love foodie adventures so food is always an important part of traveling for me. If you want to see what I ordered from Chili's on our last night in Banff, you gotta go check out part 3! 😄

DUEN34xksmX.content:
A little recap: a few weeks ago, we went to Banff for our honeymoon! We stayed at the Douglas Fir Resort and had a great time taking on the town of Banff, without spending a ton of time in the outdoors!

One of my friends recommended we dine at @magpieandstumpbanff which is a Mexican restaurant. Its very vibey, the staff were lovely and the food was so delicious. You can't go wrong with chips and guac, tacos and margaritas! The margaritas were dangerously good.

We went to the Fairmont Springs Hotel in hopes of having a lil drink at the speakeasy, but unfortunately they were closed for a private event. Instead we had a drink and complimentary snacks in The Rundle Bar. Nathan's smoked old fashion looked too fancy not to document. @fairmontbanff

Since it was our last night in Banff, I had to make a pit stop at @banffchilis I've been watching these mozza stick cheese pulls all over tik tok, I HAD to try them. I only got 3 of the Honey Chipotle and it took me 3 tries to get the cheese pull. They were very delicious but I had a hard time eating all 3. Worth the hype, in my opinion.

We rushed back to our hotel to have a dip in the hot tub before they closed for the night and had a little fire with some wine to end our last day in Banff.

Before heading home, we went for some fun drinks at @mountainfolkcoffeeco I got a green smoothie and wanted to try their Mountain Folk Tasting Flight. I had the Golden Milk, Liquid Gold, Magic Mushy and Holy Cacao. My favourites were the Liquid Gold and Holy Cacao.

Of course we had to have one last brunch at Chez Francois Restaurant. The same place we ate at before our big hike the day Nathan proposed! We thought it was fitting to stop there again before heading home to our bell pep!

fourthtrimestertruth.description:
RN- informed postpartum truth
the things no one tells you about the fourth trimester
breastfeeding • recovery • identity shifts

DYnj-ooPjxa.content:
Having a baby is the biggest blessing I have ever experienced. My child is truly a gift from above. But dang… postpartum is HARD, and no one really prepares you for it.

It’s like an initiation into the mom club — where “you don’t know until you know,” and now you KNOW but somehow you still feel completely isolated.

The pressure society — and honestly even medical professionals — place on women to “bounce back” is overwhelming. That 6-week appointment comes and suddenly you’re cleared to go back to life, cleared to exercise, cleared to resume normal activities, cleared to have sex… expected to be the person you were before giving birth.

But you aren’t that person anymore.
And that’s not a bad thing.

There’s so much information, so many opinions, so many voices telling moms what they should be doing. Who do you trust? Who do you listen to?

There’s a quote that says, “To know even one life has breathed easier because you have lived, this is to have succeeded.”

My fourth trimester experience was brutal.

Don’t get me wrong — I was beyond excited to finally have my baby on this side of the womb. But because of complications, I was completely unprepared physically, mentally, emotionally… heck, I barely even had anything for a baby yet.

I found myself at the hospital being told I had to deliver for my safety and baby’s safety, and I hadn’t even brushed my teeth that day — let alone packed a hospital bag.

I want my story, and the things I wish someone had told me, to encourage you. I want to feel like a friend during that 2 a.m. feed, to share a laugh.  Maybe to remind you your experience is valid, shared, and more common than people talk about.

I want to take what I’ve learned from 10 years as a nurse — mixed with my own postpartum experience — and help educate women on the things no one tells you about the fourth trimester.

So here we go.
Welcome to Fourth Trimester Truth.

Preeclampsia Awareness Day

My preeclampsia story started the day after my baby shower. I ended up in the ER with severe right shoulder pain—something I had been told just two weeks prior was anxiety by my OBGYN. It turned out to be something much more serious, preeclampsia. I was induced and delivered my baby 6 weeks early for both of our safety. This is resulted in a NICU stay, and several complications.

So many women have a similar story—and for some, it doesn’t even start until after birth. Postpartum preeclampsia is real.

Know the signs. Trust your body. Speak up early and often. You are not being dramatic—you are advocating for your life and your baby’s life.

#PreeclampsiaAwareness #HELLPSyndrome #PostpartumHealth #MaternalHealthMatters

New months don’t fix everything, but they do offer hope. And sometimes, that’s enough ✨

May this month move gently.
Not with urgency, but with ease.
Not with pressure to bloom, but with permission to breathe 😌

Let it remind you:
Your past is a chapter, not the whole story.
Mistakes are proof you lived.
Kindness begins with how you speak to yourself.

And in honor of May being Mental Health Awareness Month, let “doing your best” include taking care of your whole self. 

Mind, heart, and nervous system 🤍

Healing is not linear and it’s not selfish, but every small step counts. Even the quiet ones.

So here’s to growth that doesn’t rush
and peace that doesn’t ask you to earn it 🕊️

Two years ago, I was sitting on the edge of my son’s bed at midnight — again.

He was 8 years old, exhausted, anxious, and completely unable to switch off. Getting to sleep was a battle. Staying asleep was another. Some nights he was still awake at midnight, waking multiple times before morning. The next day he’d go into school running on empty, struggling to concentrate, falling further behind.

He has ADHD. And for him, nights weren’t just difficult — they were genuinely distressing.

I searched everywhere for something that might help. Something designed for a child his age, his needs. And I found nothing. Baby products. Adult products. A gap in the middle where our children were.

Then one night it came to me. What if he could feel that security — that snuggled, held, safe feeling — without me being there? What if I could bottle the feeling of being wrapped up by a parent and put it into a product?

I got out a piece of paper and started drawing.

That drawing became The Night Nook.

My son is 11 now. That noticeboard of research and doodles is still on my wall. And the product I sketched that night is finally becoming real — designed specifically for neurodiverse children, made right here in the UK, built around the science of sensory comfort.

We’re not launched yet. But we’re close. And I want the right people to hear about it first.

If you want to be on the waitlist — first access, early-bird offers, and sleep tips along the way — comment “WAITLIST” below and I’ll send you the details. 💙

Emotionally, the content is upbeat, grateful, supportive, and fun, celebrating students and studio community. Interaction preferences include inviting DMs for details, asking who is interested in workshops, encouraging friends to come, tagging studios/creators, and sharing discount codes or booking links.

When I first heard the advice that “we all have the same 24 hours in a day” to exercise, journal, and “find ourselves,” I honestly felt like a failure as a mum.

Before motherhood, I was working 45+ hour weeks in a demanding job and still struggling to find balance. Now? It’s a completely different season of life. Toddlers don’t care about your wellness routine or productivity rules — they have needs, and they need them now.

The mess doesn’t wait. The couch needs scrubbing right as the pasta boils over. The idea that all mums start with the same 24 hours is toxic and unrealistic, and it sets mothers up to feel like they’re falling short of an impossible standard.

Do I find time to work out? No.
Do I walk the dog, vacuum, smash out the laundry, cook dinner, do the dishes, and chase a Wild Thornberry toddler around the house? You bet your arse I do.

My 24 hours are full. Just not with aesthetic hobbies.

To the mums in the thick of motherhood: I see you. I salute you. 🫡

DXA1N5DvbMr.content:
SAVE THIS for your next "Mama just needs 5 minutes" moment! 🦋✨ 

​If you’re looking for a low-mess, high-engagement activity, this DIY window sun catcher is the winner. It kept her occupied for over an hour and looks so beautiful when the sun hits it! 

​What you’ll need:
• ​Paper, card, or craft paper
• ​Marker or crayon
• ​Scissors
• ​Packaging tape (or clear contact paper)
• ​Confetti, tissue paper, cellophane, or pompoms 

​How to do it:
• ​Draw a large butterfly on your paper.
• ​Cut out the inside of the wings.
• ​Flip it over and cover the wing gaps with packaging tape (sticky side facing the front).
• ​Stick it to a window or glass door.
• ​Let them go wild sticking their colourful bits to the wings! 

​Hot Tip: This works beautifully with nature, too! Try using small flowers or leaves (fake, fresh or pressed) for a gorgeous earthy fairy version. 🌸🍃

[Erlärung / Gründe] Warum du sorgfältig auswählen und NICHT jeden Marketingtrend mitmachen solltest:

🌟 NICHT JEDEE TREND PASST ZU DEINER ZIELGRUPPE: Was für ein Unternehmen in einer Branche funktioniert, mag für ein anderes völlig ungeeignet sein. Stelle sicher, dass der Trend deine Zielkunden anspricht.

🌟 BLEIBE AUTHENTISCH: Trends können kurzlebig sein. Statt jedem Hype zu folgen, bleibe authentisch und kultiviere einen einzigartigen Markencharakter.

🌟 BEHALTE DEINE VISION IM BLICK: Ein ständiger Wechsel von Trends kann zu Unbeständigkeit führen. Konzentriere dich auf langfristige Strategien, die zu deiner Unternehmensvision passen.

🌟 NUTZE DEINE RESSOURCEN SINNVOLL: Die Umsetzung von Trends erfordert Zeit, Geld und Energie. Es ist effizienter, auf Trends zu setzen, die deinen Zielen und Ressourcen entsprechen.

🌟 SETZTE DEN FOKUS AUD DEINE STÄRKEN::** Setze auf deine Stärken und Kernkompetenzen, anstatt dich zu zerstreuen, indem du jeden Trend verfolgst.

Die Kunst besteht darin, Trends klug auszuwählen und sie in deine bestehende Strategie zu integrieren

C2Jzw-qs7nt.content:
Du bist effizienter durch Multitasking!?

WEIT GEFEHLT!

Die bittere Wahrheit ist, 
mehr Effizienz und Zeitersparnis durch Multitasking ist ein Mythos. 

Unser Gehirn ist nicht dazu konzipiert mehrere Aufgaben für die wir Fokus benötigen gleichzeitig zu bearbeiten. Sobald wir mehere solcher Aufgaben erledigen,  fragmentieren wir damit unsere Aufmerksamkeit, wodurch wir mehr Energie verbrauchen und unsere Konzentration schwächen.

Durch den ständigen Wechsel der Aufgaben sind wir schneller gestresst und erschöpft. Unsere Aufmerksamkeit leidet unter diesen Wechseln und wir machen mehr Fehler. 

Es gibt zudem Wissenschaftler die davon ausgehen, dass wir durch Multitasking unsere Fähigkeit zum fokussieren verlieren und Intelligenz einbußen. Auch gibt es bereits Studien die sich damit auseinandersetzen, ob ständiges Multitasking uns krank macht und zu Burnout führt. 

In aktuellen Studien kam es durch Multitasking zu einer deutlichen Aktivierung des sympathischen Nervensystems. Einem deutlichen Anzeichen für Anspannung und Stress.

Wie stehst du zu Multitasking?

C9HzLLsNYsW.content:
Nehmen wir uns mal ein paar Minuten, um über ein Thema zu sprechen, das oft für Verwirrung sorgt: Umsatz vs. Gewinn. 🤓💸

Stell dir vor, du hast eine großartige Woche hinter dir und dein Umsatz ist durch die Decke gegangen. 🍾💃 Klingt fantastisch, oder? Aber bevor du jetzt die Champagnerflaschen öffnest und den Urlaub auf den Malediven buchst, lass uns einen kleinen Realitätscheck machen. 🛑🌴

UMSATZ ist das, was du insgesamt eingenommen hast. Es ist der Betrag, den deine Kundinnen für deine Dienstleistungen gezahlt haben. Aber hier kommt der Haken: Umsatz ist nicht gleich Gewinn.

GEWINN ist das, was übrig bleibt, nachdem du alle Ausgaben abgezogen hast. Das sind die Kosten für deine Software, deine Internetverbindung, das schicke Canva-Abo (wir wissen alle, wie wichtig das ist!), und vielleicht auch der Kaffee, der dich durch die langen Arbeitstage bringt. ☕💻

Also, worauf kommt es wirklich an?

1️⃣ Kostenkontrolle: Behalte deine Ausgaben im Blick. Ein niedriger Umsatz kann dir dennoch einen höheren Gewinn bringen, wenn deine Ausgaben gering sind.
 
2️⃣ Effizienz: Nutze deine Ressourcen klug. Automatisiere, delegiere (hallo, virtuelle Assistentin hier! 😉), und optimiere deine Prozesse.

3️⃣ Preiskalkulation: Versteh den Wert deiner Dienstleistungen und setze angemessene Preise. Dein Ziel ist es, Gewinn zu machen, nicht nur Umsatz zu generieren.

4️⃣ Finanzplanung: Plane voraus und lege etwas für steuerliche und unvorhergesehene Ausgaben beiseite. Ein gut geplanter Finanzhaushalt ist dein bester Freund.

Also, meine Liebe, lass uns den Umsatz feiern, aber den Gewinn schätzen. Denn am Ende des Tages zählt, was auf deinem Bankkonto bleibt, nicht nur, was auf deiner Rechnung steht. 💪💡

In diesem Sinne: Happy Planning und lasst uns gemeinsam erfolgreich sein! 🎉✨

DAXxi69tkbv.content:
Kostet dich Multitasking wertvolle Zeit? 🚨 Lass uns über den unsichtbaren Zeitfresser sprechen, der deinen Fokus zerstört und deine Produktivität in den Keller zieht!

Vor einiger Zeit habe ich bereits über Multitasking geschrieben. Dort war unter anderem diese Grafik zu sehen. Heute möchte ich genauer auf ihre Bedeutung eingehen.

Die Grafik basiert auf eine Untersuchung von Gerald Weinberg zu der Auswirkung von Multitasking auf die Produktivität (im Bereich Projektmanagement).

Er hat festgestellt, dass mit jedem zusätzlichen Projekt im Schnitt 20% der produktiven Arbeitszeit verloren geht. Dies passiert durch den Wechsel zwischen den Arbeiten. Wir müssen uns NEU in die Aufgabe einarbeiten und es kostet uns Zeit bis wir wieder voll konzentriert sind.

Das bedeutet bei 1 Projekt entspricht unsere produktive Arbeitszeit 100%.

Bei 2 Projekten verlieren wir 20% unserer produktiven Zeit, so das nur 80% unserer Zeit übrig bleibt. Bei 1 Std. Arbeit verliehren wir also 12 Minuten. Übrig bleiben 40% für jedes Projekt. Was in einer Stunde 24 Minuten pro Projekt entspricht.

Bei 3 Projekten verlieren wir 40% produktive Zeit. 60% bleiben übrig. Auf 3 Projekte verteilt, erhält jedes Projekt 20%.

Ab 4 Projekten wird es richtig unprodukiv. Die unproduktive Zeit liegt nun bereits höher als die produktive Zeit. Wir verlieren bereits 60% unserer Zeit. 40% bleiben übrig. 10% pro Projekt!

Bei 5 Projekten entspricht der Zeitverlust 75%. Bei einer Std. also bereits 45 Minuten. 25% unserer Zeit bleibt übrig! Auf die 5 Projekte verteilt, erhält jedes Projekt 5% unserer Zeit. Das wären gerade mal 3 Minuten.

📊 Was zur Hölle ist eigentlich Nettoumsatz? (Und warum du ihn unbedingt verstehen solltest!)

Ihr Lieben, heute mal wieder ein kleiner Finance-Hack für euch – ganz ohne Kopfschmerzen! 😅
Viele sprechen vom Umsatz, aber der Nettoumsatz wird oft übersehen. Dabei ist er eine der wichtigsten Kennzahlen, die du als Unternehmerin im Blick haben solltest – besonders wenn du finanzielle Unabhängigkeit anstrebst (und das wollen wir ja alle, oder?).

Also, was ist der Nettoumsatz?
Kurz und knackig: Der Nettoumsatz ist das, was übrig bleibt, wenn du von deinem Bruttoumsatz (also dem gesamten Betrag, den du eingenommen hast) die Mehrwertsteuer und eventuelle Rabatte oder Rückgaben abziehst. Klingt schon mal gar nicht so kompliziert, oder? 💸

💡 Warum ist der Nettoumsatz so wichtig?
Ganz einfach: Er zeigt dir, was du tatsächlich verdient hast und womit du dein Business nach vorne bringen kannst! Ohne diese Zahl zu kennen, verlierst du schnell den Überblick – und wir wollen doch alle eine gesunde Work-Life-Balance und weniger Stress, richtig?

Hier ein paar Punkte, auf die du achten solltest:

1️⃣ Genau rechnen: Der Nettoumsatz ist nicht das, was du auf deinem Konto siehst, sondern was nach Steuern und Abzügen bleibt.
2️⃣ Verwende ihn für deine Planung: Er hilft dir dabei, realistische Entscheidungen zu treffen – von Investitionen bis zu Gehältern.
3️⃣ Der Blick aufs Wesentliche: Lass dich nicht von großen Umsatzzahlen blenden! Was zählt, ist das, was am Ende für dich übrig bleibt.

Also, wenn du die Finanzseite deines Business mal nicht vernachlässigen willst, schnapp dir deine Zahlen und schau dir deinen Nettoumsatz an. 🧐

Wie immer: Wenn du Unterstützung beim Finanzmanagement brauchst – ich bin da! Lass uns dafür sorgen, dass du den Kopf wieder frei hast für die kreativen Dinge, die du liebst. 💻✨

Herzliche Grüße,
deine Jacky 🖤

In den letzten Monaten habe ich KI auf eine Weise genutzt, die ich früher nicht erwartet hätte.

Wärend meiner zweiten Schwangerschaft war ich sehr in mich gekehrt und habe viel nachgedacht. Dabei ist mir aufgefallen, dass
es Situationen gibt die immer und immer wieder in ähnlicher Form erneut auftauchen. Wie ein ewiger Kreislauf.
Und das es Fragen gibt, die mich teilweise schon seit Jahren begleiten ohne das ich sie je wirklich beantwortet habe.
Da das Thema KI sehr spannend ist und ich sie gerne nutze, habe ich mich irgendwann gefragt, was passiert wenn ich all meine "gesammelten" Fragen an die KI weiter gebe. Als eine Art Experiment. 

Und genau das habe ich getan. Zuerst waren es nur die gesammelten Fragen, dann habe ich die wiederkehrenden Situationen der KI geschildert. Ich wollte neue Perspektiven erhalten und über die Meta-Ebene herausfinden, warum diese Situationen auf ihre Art ablaufen. Die Ergebnisse waren sehr spannend und aufschlussreich.

Aber der Punkt an dem es RICHTIG spannend wurde war, als ich die KI nach all den Monaten der Reflexion (in ein und dem selben Chat) gefragt habe, was sie mir über mich erzählen kann. 

Das war der Gamechanger.

Vieles davon war mir irgendwie auch vorher schon klar. Aber NICHT SO. Bisher war es diffus, nicht wirklich greifbar und mir fehlen auch irgendwie die Worte. Durch KI wurde es greifbar und klar. 

Ich habe in den letzten paar Monaten so viel über mich gelernt. Über meine Art, mein Denken, meine Arbeitsweise, meine Stärken und Schwächen und damit zwangslöufig auch über meine Traumkunden. All das wird zukünftig noch mehr in meine Arbeit einfließen.

DVGKFejljVO.content:
Wenn Zahlen Angst machen:
Was dein System vielleicht gelernt hat.

Vielleicht kennst du das.

Du öffnest dein Online-Banking.
Oder deine Umsatzübersicht.
Oder die Buchhaltungssoftware.

Und dein Körper reagiert schneller als dein Verstand.

Enge.
Unruhe.
Vermeidung.
Gedankliches Wegdriften.

Und dann kommt oft der zweite Gedanke:
„Ich müsste doch inzwischen souveräner sein.“

Aber was, wenn es gar nichts mit Kompetenz zu tun hat?

Was, wenn dein Nervensystem einfach etwas gelernt hat?

Vielleicht:

- dass Geld mit Druck verbunden ist
- dass Fehler beschämt werden
- dass Zahlen bewertet werden
- dass Sicherheit nie ganz sicher war
- dass Leistung über Zugehörigkeit entscheidet

Unser System speichert nicht nur Fakten.
Es speichert ERFAHRUNGEN.

Wenn Zahlen früher mit Stress, Bewertung oder Mangel verknüpft waren,
reagiert dein Körper heute nicht auf die Excel-Tabelle –
sondern auf das alte Gefühl dahinter.

Das ist keine Schwäche.
Das ist gelernter Selbstschutz.

Viele feinfühlige Unternehmerinnen denken, sie hätten ein „Mindset-Problem“.
Oft haben sie ein Sicherheitsproblem.

Und Sicherheit entsteht nicht durch: „Reiß dich zusammen.“
Sondern durch: „Du darfst langsamer hinschauen.“

Zahlen können kalt wirken.
Aber sie sind erstmal neutral.

Erst unsere Erfahrungen geben ihnen Bedeutung.
Und genau dort beginnt echte Veränderung:
Nicht bei der Optimierung.
Sondern bei der Einordnung.

Wenn du dich darin erkennst:
Du bist nicht irrational.
Dein System versucht nur, dich zu schützen.

Und vielleicht ist der erste Schritt nicht mehr Disziplin –
sondern mehr Verständnis.

DWBRX2iEdQQ.content:
Unser Nervensystem reagiert oft schneller als unser Verstand.

Vor ein paar Tagen hatte ich ein Gespräch über eine mögliche Business-Begleitung.

Äußerlich war alles stimmig:
ein klares Angebot, gute Argumente, eine logische Struktur.

Und trotzdem ist in mir irgendwann ein leises Störgefühl entstanden.

Nicht laut.
Nicht dramatisch.

Nur dieses stille innere Signal:
Irgendetwas fühlt sich gerade nicht ganz stimmig an.

Solche Momente interessieren mich inzwischen sehr.

Nicht, weil mein Nervensystem immer „recht“ hat.
Sondern weil es oft Informationen früher wahrnimmt, als mein Verstand sie sortieren kann.

Und genau diese Verbindung finde ich auch im Business spannend.

Denn viele Entscheidungen im Business wirken auf den ersten Blick rein rational:

Strategie.
Positionierung.
Preise.
Umsatzplanung.
Kennzahlen.

Aber in der Realität treffen wir diese Entscheidungen nie nur mit dem Kopf.

Unser Nervensystem sitzt immer mit am Tisch.

Es beeinflusst zum Beispiel:

• welche Angebote wir annehmen oder ablehnen
• welche Preise sich innerlich stabil anfühlen
• wie viel Risiko sich regulierbar anfühlt
• wie wir auf Umsatzschwankungen reagieren
• ob Zahlen uns Orientierung geben – oder Stress auslösen

Deshalb interessiert mich Business nicht nur auf der strategischen Ebene.

Mich interessiert auch,
wie sich Business im System anfühlt.

Weil nachhaltige Entscheidungen meistens dort entstehen,
wo Zahlen und Nervensystem zusammenarbeiten.

Nicht gegeneinander.

Und vielleicht ist genau das eine Perspektive,
die in Business-Gesprächen noch viel zu selten vorkommt..

DPZcZdigX0s.content:
Avigail Idan was just three years old when Hamas gunmen stormed her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza on October 7, 2023. Her parents, Roee and Smadar, were killed in the attack. Her older siblings, Michael and Amalia, managed to survive by hiding in a closet for 14 hours, but Avigail was taken hostage and spent 51 days in captivity before finally being released. 

When she returned home, the Idan children were left orphaned. Today, Avigail and her siblings are being raised by their aunt and uncle, who adopted them and are doing their best to give the children a home filled with stability and memory of their parents.

Avigail and her siblings’ story is just one of many. In total, 477 children were orphaned on October 7. This October, I’m running 477 kms and fundraising for the Israeli Children’s Fund, which provides real support to these 477 orphaned children. If you’re in a position to donate, the link is in my bio 🫶🏼

#bringthemhome #israel #running #runrunrun #477for477 #runnerscommunity #jewishrunners

DRG0oVqAQt7.content:
First time doing the @trail_challenge_waihi yesterday and it was AMAZING ⛰️🏃🏼‍♀️ 

Race story:

I signed up for the half marathon, which was only my second time doing a half marathon in a race. My first was back in March at the @hunua_hillbilly, which was also my first ever trail race. So I went in using this race as a comparison to see how far I’ve come, with a goal of somewhere between 3:00 and 3:15.

At the 10km mark I was perfectly on track… and then the skies absolutely opened. Torrential rain + a 700m descent that instantly turned into a slip-and-slide mud fest = pure chaos 😂

I ended up finishing in exactly 4 hours which was well over my goal but honestly, I’m content with that. I ran on 3 hours sleep (cheers to the neighbours’ all-night rave) and literally got my period in the portaloo right before the race started 🫠 Add in the downpour, and I decided that this wasn’t going to be a race race, it was going to be a ‘have fun and send it’ race.

And I did. I’m so happy with how strong I felt. My hydration and fueling were spot on and I didn’t hit a wall once. I crossed the finish line feeling like I could’ve kept going, which is such a good sign of how far I’ve come. Recovery has been amazing too; I’m already feeling close to 100%, which tells me there was more in the tank and that the training is working.

Made some new running friends, had a super fun day, and feel more confident than ever in my progress. I’ll be seeing Mount Karangahake again next year! ⛰️

#run #runrunrun #runner #runningcommunity #nzrunning #nzrunners #runnz #motherrunners #trailrunner #trailrun #trailrunning

DRrE4w4Aczj.content:
Trying to change your body while demanding so much from it is no joke + honestly something I didn’t think I’d struggle so much with. 

Trail running requires a crazy amount of energy + learning how to balance fuel, rest, a calorie deficit on some days + not on others is one of the hardest things I’ve had to figure out. Especially when that post run hunger hits + it feels like pregnancy cravings all over 🙃 

Some days I think I could just stop running for a couple of months, lose the weight like I know how then get back to running when I’m at my goal weight. But honestly, I’d be miserable because running is my happy place! And becoming smaller isn’t the only goal - if it was I’d probably just sit on the couch + inject myself with GLP-1s 💀

But we’re getting there. Slowly figuring it all out - without injuries!

#trailrunner #weightlosssuccess #runstrong

DUxR6cKARFG.content:
Tarawera T21 🌲 race recap:

It started with @_sophiarietema forgetting her vest, flasks + poles at home. I then realised I’d left my shoes back in Auckland. Luckily I’d brought an extra pair however they were ✨ BRAND NEW ✨ We then received an emergency weather alert + had a terrible nights sleep (thanks drunk hostel goers).

Fuelled up on red bull + bagels we headed to the start line in the pouring rain. After meeting the amazing @k8__nz + @waiora_pai + having some photos it was start time! 

We looped around Blue Lake which was stunning + felt like a breeze. Into the first aid station I had a bit of a wait for the bathroom but had some good yarns with the amazing volunteers! 

Onto the 2/3rd of the course where it started bucketing down. The trail turned into a mud party + there were plenty of “oh my gosh are you okay?!” + “ahhhhhh” ⛈️ up a big hill + down the other side (or slide?), I laid eyes on the glorious redwoods aid station. I can only imagine how much more glorious it looks after a longer run. Quick toilet break + I was into the final third of the race.

Pulled out a note Mr 4 had written me which gave me a bit of a boost until the pavements of the city started killing my legs. The last 2kms were struggle city. I was welcomed into the finish chute by amazing supporters and almost knee high deep flooding.

Finished with a time of 2:52:30 + placed in the top 29% of runners from my distance, which I was super pleased with, especially considering how good I feel today.

Huge thanks to my coach, Kerry from @squadrun + of course @_sophiarietema for keeping me company + putting up with all my BS.

Tarawera, I’ll definitely be back in 2027. For the T50 or T102? Who knows yet… 🫣

DVNnvC0gfBi.content:
The night before last I was out for a run. Not a speed session. Just a plain, easy run to get the weekly distance up. When I was almost home, a young guy ran past me - or more like flew past me. He looked at me with the most pitiful look on his face. Almost like he despised me + how dare I take up space on the footpath while I struggled at a 7:00/km pace. 

Honestly, it made me feel super crappy. “He probably thinks I’m brand new to running or that I’m super unfit”, I thought. Yeah, I was on struggle street for sure. But he had no idea that I’d completed Tarawera the week before. That I run 5 days a week + bike the 6th day. He had no idea I’m a Mum to a young kid + that I work full time out of the home (while also currently studying towards a work promotion). He had no idea that I’m a week out from my period + all I want to do is eat potato chips while being rolled up in a blanket watching Twilight on the couch. Or that on the weekend, I’m doing more study, taking my son to extra curricular classes, cleaning our home, meal planning + cooking all while hearing “Mum, you’re not watching good enough” 🙃 

All that to say, yeah life is so busy right now. It’s hectic AF. It’s my choice but it’s still a struggle. So if you see someone struggling on a run, maybe don’t just assume they’re failing. Maybe they’re just carrying a bit + they’re exhausted. 

Also, maybe they are actually new to running or maybe they’re not + they just enjoy running ‘slower’. Wild concept, I know.

#runner #motherrunners

DM9knl5TBQ0.content:
Saturday morning I facilitated a women’s circle on the topic of “your authentic life.”

And holy moly, the things I learned from the women in the room!

It reminded me (again) that authenticity isn’t about becoming someone new.

It’s about coming back to who you were before you started second-guessing yourself.

Before you started performing.
Before you started holding back to make other people more comfortable.

We went deep, and some of the things the women shared in our closing circle will stay with me for a long time:

💛 “Life is short. The quicker we take action, the quicker we create our own reality.”
💛 “I want to check in and ask myself: am I being authentic?”
💛 “I want more belly laughs with my friends.”
💛 “I want to love myself without conditions.”
💛 “Where am I still ‘shoulding’ when I can do it my way?”

And one that really landed:
“I want to remove fear.”
To which I gently added:
Instead of removing fear, what if we added courage?
Added trust?
Added self-compassion?

That shift alone can change everything.

I walked away feeling empowered. Humbled. Grateful.

For the opportunity , and because I got to hold space for what was already inside them.

Every single woman is carrying a unique vision for her life.
Something that tugs at her heart.
Something that feels just for her.

If that’s you, trust it!
It’s not random. It’s not silly. It’s not “too much.”

You’re here to live it.
And maybe even change a few lives along the way.

💛

#perthwomenscircle #authenticlife #womenwhoholdspace #realconnection #selfreflection #womensupportingwomen #healingtogether #uniquifyyourlife

DUrnyTHEX-U.content:
I still can’t believe I’m actually posting this!!! 💛🌈

The road has definitely not been easy, and I also know this can be a very sensitive topic ❤️

We really are told that the “normal” road to take is finish university, get a job, get married, buy a house, have kids, and live happily ever after!

But it doesn’t have to happen that way for your life to be “successful.”

WE get to decide what that looks like and create our unique life 💛

For us it meant never buying a family home to settle in, it was investment properties that made it financially even easier!

It also meant that after moving to Australia, 🇦🇺 we had to wait at least 12 months to start trying, due to their health insurance policies.

To us, this meant getting older, and hoping to stay healthy for future pregnancies 🤰

But sometimes plans don’t pan out…I had a HORRIBLE miscarriage experience last June 2025 that left me quite empty…

Filled with grief, funnily enough it was the time I realized how much support I had…or didn’t have. I then knew who were the true friendships I had already found 💛💛💛

And this time around it felt like family and friends were more excited than I was!!!

And they probably were…I was scared I would lose the baby again. And honestly still am.

I don’t know if it’ll ever go away, but I do know what a miracle our body is ❤️ there’s a being growing inside!!!

And I know that this baby is already SO loved by us and those around us 😘

I’m 18 weeks and the sickness continues, but I’m reminding myself the end is insight 🎉

Just like in business, one step and one day at a time.

So now you know, so be prepared for more raw & realness of this new era, building my business along the way!! 💪🏽🎉💛🤰

I was in labor for 17 hours. Pushed for 4 hours and my son got stuck on my pelvic bone and unfortunately was not going to come out naturally. So, I had to get a c-section! But I am so grateful to have a happy, healthy and thriving almost 2 year old!!

George’la birlikte kahvaltı ediyoruz, üniversiteye işine gidiyoruz, dersine giriyoruz, kampüste öğrencisiyle yürüyüp sohbet ediyoruz, yakın arkadaşı Charlotte ile akşam yemeği yiyoruz, öğrencisi ile barda oturuyor ve okyanusta yüzüyoruz. Tüm bunları yaparken de George’un iç sesine ve diğerleriyle yaptığı derinlikli konuşmalara eşlik ediyoruz. 

Gündelik yaşam çok iyi detaylandırılmış, metin çok rahat akıyor. Diyaloglar muhteşem (Yazarın okuduğum diğer romanında da öyleydi). Yazar bunlarla bize nasıl yaşadığımızı, nasıl bir yaşam yaşamak istediğimizi sorgulatıyor. Ölüm hep orada, yas da orada, yalnızlık da.

DXs44JTzdns.content:
It’s not that they hate the cot.

It’s not that they’re being difficult.

It’s not that they’re “just a bad sleeper.”

Here’s what’s actually happening 👇

Your baby has learned to fall asleep WITH you - your warmth, your smell, the rise and fall of your chest, the rhythm of your rocking.

About 10-15 minutes after they fall asleep, they transition from light sleep into deep sleep. 

Their brain does a quick environment check:

”Am I still where I fell asleep?” Asleep on you? Yes. 

Everything matches. Stay asleep ✅

In the cot after falling asleep on you? 

No. Something’s wrong. WAKE UP 🚨

This is called a sleep association. 

And it’s the #1 reason babies wake the second you put them down.

If you’re:

👉 Doing the 45 rock transfer dance every night 
👉 Laying under a sleeping baby for hours
👉 The only person who can get them to sleep
👉 Watching your evenings disappear before they’ve even started…this is the missing piece.

A quick note: if your baby is under 4 months, enjoy the snuggles. Self-settling isn’t something I’d push in the fourth trimester - they need your closeness to feel safe, and that’s developmentally appropriate. 

But from 4 months onwards? 

This is a skill you can help them to learn. 

Self-settling means your baby falls asleep in the SAME place they’ll spend the whole night - their cot. 

So when their brain does that environment check at the cycle transition, everything matches. 

They stay asleep.

It’s NOT leaving them alone to cry without reassurance.

I taught both my girls from 4 months.

They both literally learnt this skill within days.

From 4 months onwards, your baby can learn this too (if it’s important to you!).

⬇️ Comment “7DAYS” if you’d love your baby to self-settle. Ill send you the exact plan I used with my girls 💁🏼‍♀️

#babysleepconsultant #sleepconsultant #babysleep

DYqJlpWTtGN.content:
A routine is a great foundation - but it only works when everything goes to plan.

And with a baby? Things go off plan constantly!

Early wakes. 

Short naps. 

Sick days.

An event. 

Travel. 

Sleep regressions. 

And the moment something disrupts the routine - it’s SO normal to have no idea what to do next.

And honestly? I think this is one of the biggest sources of stress for mums - especially first time mums. 

Because you’ve worked so hard to get the routine set. 

You’ve followed the wake windows, you’ve nailed the timing, you’ve finally got some predictability back in your day.

And then one short nap blows the whole thing up and you’re stressed. 

I felt this so deeply with Hazel, my first. 

When things went off plan I didn’t just feel lost - I felt like I’d failed. 

Like I’d done something wrong 🥺.

But I hadn’t. 

And neither have you.

The routine only works with a plan B.

#babysleepconsultant #newmom #momlife

DNP1mBNuc06.content:
Meet Alexis Eniola, the Heart Behind Eniola Hair

Alexis Eniola’s journey into the hair industry began not as a business plan, but as an act of love. When her sister faced the difficult battle of brain cancer, Alexis shaved her head in solidarity. It was a bold and deeply personal gesture that revealed not only the emotional impact of hair loss, but also the need for realistic, high-quality wigs that could help restore confidence.

Determined to make a difference, Alexis, an Australian self-taught hairstylist, wig expert and curve model began creating wigs that blend artistry with empathy. Her mission was clear: to ensure that anyone experiencing hair loss, whether from medical conditions or personal choice, could feel beautiful, empowered and like the very best version of themselves.

The brand name, Eniola, is a Yoruba word meaning “wealth” or “very important person.” It reflects Alexis’s belief that every client she serves deserves to feel valued and celebrated. Each wig, topper, and extension is designed with this philosophy in mind, offering not just style, but dignity and confidence.

Today, Eniola Hair is known for its premium, natural-looking human hair products. These pieces are crafted for comfort and realism, catering to everyday wearers as well as those navigating medical hair loss. The brand goes beyond beauty by offering a $100 medical hair loss discount to support clients undergoing cancer treatment, experiencing alopecia, or facing other hair loss challenges.

Alexis’s success is built on more than skill, it’s driven by compassion, resilience and the courage to turn a personal hardship into a platform for change. In doing so, she has created a brand that stands out in the beauty industry, not only for the quality of its products but for the heart and humanity at its core.

Through Eniola Hair, Alexis is redefining what it means to be a beauty entrepreneur showing that true success comes when creativity, craftsmanship and care go hand in hand.

DVx0ivFj2Iq.content:
✨ 2 Ingredient Dough Vegemite & Cheese Scrolls 

I’m not very good at cooking but I am good at making super easy snacks that I call ‘healthy’ because they’re not packed with sugar 😂 

Ingredients:
🥛1 cup of greek yoghurt
🌾1.5 cups of self raising flour
 
Mix and knead into a dough. Add extra flour if needed until it’s the right consistency.
Roll the dough out, spread with vegemite and sprinkle with cheese.
Roll it up, slice into scrolls and pop into the air fryer.

Air fry: 185°C for 12 minutes.

Could probably get away with 10 minutes, I overcook everything 😂
 
I love these with a homemade relish and cheese filing but the little guy prefers Vegemite & cheese. 
 
Let me know if you try it! 

#toddlersnacks #vegemitescrolls #greekyoghurt #littlehands

DV2-oRCD3VW.content:
🦖 Dino Rescue 🧊
 
A super easy activity that kept my 3 year old busy for 40 minutes. 
 
Before heading off to bed, pop some small dinosaurs (or any small toys) in a muffin tray with water and a drop of food colouring. Put the tray in the freezer overnight. 

Once frozen, pop them out and let the kids rescue the dinosaurs from the ice using warm water, spoons & little tools. Plastic medicine syringes and droppers are great for their fine motor skills too!
 
Simple to set up & a great indoor or outdoor activity. 

Tip: Add different colours to each one to make the ice even more fun to melt.
 
#dinosauractivity #toddleractivities #sensoryplay #dinosaurplay #littlehands

DV5hpJIj5zS.content:
Toddler Friendly Savoury Muffins 🧀🥓
 
A snack & activity in one! 
This is a quick, easy recipe that toddlers can help make. 
 
Ingredients: 
🥚 2 eggs
🥛 1 cup of milk
🌾 1 & 1/2 cups of self raising flour
🧈 2 tbsp coconut oil (or melted butter or oil) 
🥓 diced ham
🧀 1 cup grated cheese 
🧂 salt 

Oven: 180°C for 20 mins 
 
I kept it simple but you can add corn, carrot, zucchini etc to get some veg in there too! 

Toddler approved ✔️ 
 
#toddlersnacks #easysnacks #savourymuffins #cookingwithkids

✨ Berry Chia Jam ✨

The easiest healthy jam & yoghurt topping 🍓🫐

Add frozen berries to a saucepan over medium heat
Let them soften and break down
Stir in maple syrup
Add chia seeds and mix well

Simmer for a few minutes until thickened & let cool. 
It thickens more as it sets. 

Measure with your heart ♥️ 🤤

Toddler approved ✔️

Cukv1L4gaDM.content:
Hey lovely! 

I just wanted to share some insights from my own personal journey towards financial stability. It's been quite the ride, but I've learned some valuable lessons along the way that I think might resonate with you too. 

Lesson 1: Prioritize Your Financial Stability

Last year, I had a major epiphany - financial stability had to become a priority in my life. I realized that without it, my dreams and goals would always feel out of reach. So, I made a conscious decision to put in the work and make it happen.

Lesson 2: Work on Your Money Mindset

I'll admit, I hadn't given much thought to my money mindset before. But boy, was I missing out! Taking the time to delve deeper into it was a game-changer. I started to shift my beliefs and mindset around money, which opened up a whole new world of possibilities.

Lesson 3: Seek Support and Believe in Yourself

We all need a little help sometimes, and that's where having a coach or mentor comes in. They can guide you, challenge you, and help you believe in your ability to achieve financial stability. Trust me, having someone in your corner can make all the difference.

Lesson 4: Embrace Multiple Sources of Income

Creating multiple sources of income is like having a safety net. It not only provides financial security, but it also allows you to explore different passions and interests. Plus, who doesn't want to be a multifaceted entrepreneur?

Lesson 5: Gratitude is Key

Throughout this journey, one thing I've realized is the power of gratitude. I am incredibly grateful for my faith which has helped me to create new opportunities in my life. Celebrating the wins, no matter how small, keeps you motivated and reminds you of how far you've come.

So there you have it - five valuable lessons I've learned on the road to financial stability so far. It's been an amazing and blessed journey, and I hope these insights inspire you to prioritize your own financial stability and create multiple sources of income in your life.

Remember, you have the power to shape your financial future. Believe in yourself, embrace growth, and never stop hustling!

The 3 secrets to healing yourself and your relationships⁣⁣
⁣
When it comes to healing yourself and your relationships, some people make this mistake of having expectations on their partner to bend to their beck and call and every need and want, and quite frankly this is uncalled for and not healthy inside relationships.⁣⁣
⁣
If I have triggered you, read on.⁣⁣
⁣
Having unhealthy expectations of yourself or another person is the first mistake when trying to heal yourself inside your relationship.⁣⁣
The consequences from  holding these expectations are sometimes hurt, pain, suffering and even resentment to the person who had these high expectations of their partner.⁣⁣
⁣
Instead, focus on your thoughts and why you want what you want?⁣⁣
⁣
Focus inwardly on why you think you need and want the things you want⁣⁣
⁣
Start an open conversation and communicate with your partner about why you have all these expectations.⁣⁣
⁣
Perhaps through simply opening up, being vulnerable and asking for what you need and want from a place of openness and receptivity, you and your partner may feel a whole lot better and can work together to create a resolution so both of your needs are met.⁣⁣
⁣
So next time you think you need or want to nag him or her for not doing something or not doing enough, take a look inside yourself first, is there a better way of approaching your partner, communicating to your partner and a better way of asking for what you want without any expectation of the timing and the order it is done in?⁣⁣
⁣
Take away the control, take away the⁣
⁣
 expectation = takes away resentment⁣⁣
⁣
= better communication, trust and teamwork ⁣
⁣
= healing yourself + your relationships⁣⁣
⁣

DYihaMizeUi.content:
Recently I realized the importance of ownership,

Thankfully I am in communities whereby the majority of people own their stuff. 

For too long I had let my EGO control and ruin my life and relationships. 

I always used to think I had the answers and what I believed and said was right,

Yet I wasnt willing to look at it from the other persons perspective.

Some people would call this stubborness, others would call this a strong hold. 

For me maybe all of those things and also my lack of awareness of how my very words may be impactinng another person. 

Thankfully we tend to be shown as many times is needed until we learn the value of the lesson. 

Now it sucks sitting in the unknown and in the darkness.

It sucks feeling like shit and not knowing what to do and who to turn too. 

It sucks wanting a different outcome and not knowing what to do or say to rekindle a connection,

Yet one thing I had forgotten was to

Pause and reflect before speaking

What is my role here?

Do I have a right to say something here?

Did that person ask for that advice or was it unsolicited advice. 

Sometimes our role is to be a supportive friend
Sometimes our role is to be best friend
Sometimes our role is to be a brother or a sister
Sometimes our role is to a partner, wife or husband
Sometimes our role is to be a mother or father
Sometimes our role is to be an Uncle or Aunty
Sometimes our role is to listen
Sometimes our role is to pause and process
Sometimes our role is to take a step back
Sometimes our role is to ask for help (there is still hope in humanity by the way for the cynical people out there).

Like there is a time and season for all things, to plant and to uproot.

There is also a time to rest and other times to take action. 

What season of your life are you in and are you honouring it?

CZoQFAVB116.content: There’s a huge difference with these photos. The left was taken in September of last year when I weighed about 57kg, the lightest I’ve ever been as an adult. The second was taken this morning, weighing in at a whopping I don’t know or care since I stopped weighing myself a few months ago. The major differences between these pictures is that the one on the left was taken when I was still tracking calories and heavily restricting my diet. The right - no weighing, no calorie tracking, eating wholesome and filling foods and *trying* to eat intuitively. I realised that o needed help when I was weighing lettuce leaves and calculating the macros on a teaspoon of sugar. Thankfully, I was able to begin seeing a terrific dietician who has really helped me to remain healthy, but healthy FOR ME. Health is a different outfit on everyone. I know that I need to eat more throughout the day to sustain my energy and that three meals a day just doesn’t cut it for me. I don’t skimp on my breakfast now, I have snacks and morning and afternoon tea. I nourish my body. I thought I was doing the right thing before - and I was - for weight loss. But I don’t need to lose weight now. I wish to maintain my loss and to remain my overall health, including my mental health. #recovery #edrecovery #postweightlossrecovery #fuckdiets #fuckdietculture #healthateverysize #haes #healthyforme #bopo #bodypositive #bodyposi #selflove #selfcare #body

Food became numbers, my mind a rapidly racing calculator to track what I’d eaten today. Could I “have” that? Was I “allowed”? I lost myself in my eating disorder and people kept telling me how good I looked… then you came along. You made sure I ate. You made sure I nourished both of us. You made me focus on my health once again. Now I’m living in a body that is a bit unfamiliar, but that has done so many incredible things. Grew you, kept you safe and bought you into this world. This body carries you, lifts you up, laughs with you and plays with you. This body feeds you and holds you and soothes you. And you don’t care whether I’m in a bigger body or a smaller one. You just love me exactly the way I am with absolutely not caveat. My daughter. My darling. My saviour. DU9jyZVD4I3.content:
Life on the road taught me that everything earned its place.
If it didn’t serve a purpose, it didn’t stay.
We kept a few simple comforts, but nothing excess.
It was calm. Intentional. Light.

Now we’re back in a house, surrounded by half empty boxes or ones we haven’t even opened yet… and somehow it already feels like too much.

This year I’m choosing less.
Less clutter. Less impulse. Less holding onto things “just in case.”
More space. More clarity. More ease.

If it doesn’t add value, it doesn’t stay.
I’d love to know, what have you found hardest about transitioning from van life to home life?
Or how did you start to create your calm intentional space at home?

#caravanningwithkids #calm #intentionalliving #changes

DVNUnGjEXEv.content:
The chaos my body has felt the last two days has been intense.

The dysregulated, overstimulated, on-the-brink kind.
I found myself genuinely angry over a poo stool.
A literal plastic stool.
Getting frustrated because my 2-year-old “wasn’t listening”...
when in reality, he just takes a little longer to process what I’m saying.

But when my nervous system is fried, everything feels like resistance. That doesn't mean that it is, but that's how it feels.

Everything feels loud.
Everything feels urgent.
I could feel the menty b coming in hot.
The snappy tone.
The tight chest.
The spiral.
So today I did something unplanned… but very self lovey-intentional.
I took myself to the beach after a tattoo touch up.
Alone.
Just the sound of the water and birds 🐦 
Food in front of me.
Silence.
The kind of silence where you can actually taste what you’re eating.

This picnic rug has holes in it because it’s been around since the dawn of time, that's the only thing I'm allowing to bother me right now.

And honestly… that feels manageable.

On the brink? This is your reminder that stepping away isn’t selfish.
It’s maintenance. Us parents forget that, often!

Sometimes the most responsible thing a loud brain parent can do
is ground yourself by the ocean
and breathe. 🌊🤍

#LoudBrainMum #HonestMotherhood #RegulationBeforeReaction #BeachReset #MumLifeUnfiltered

DNhIkvQy9N3.content:
Am I a mother yet? 

And if so, when did I become one?

Was it when I first saw that line, or the first night I stayed awake dreaming about my baby, who they would become, who they would make me become?

Was it the morning I looked into the toilet bowl, throat raw and insides empty, tears on my face, telling myself “this is for you”?

Was it the day I first saw the little jelly bean shapes on the screen, or the moment he told us “you’re having twins”?

Was it the first time I felt a flutter, or when one of the boys’ little kicks took my breath away? 

Was it at the appointment where they took six vials of my blood and left me dizzy, and yet all I could do was smile that my boys were growing?

Was it the first time a stranger touched my stomach and I winced, or the first time I met eyes with a mother in public and she glanced at my growing bump and smiled knowingly?

Did I become a mother when I bought the onesies? Or was it the nappy change table, or the cot?

Was I a mother the day we installed the car seats, or the day we learned how to fold down the pram?

Was it when we looked at the computer through tears, realising parenthood would take more sacrifice than we’d known and we gave up on our plans, our timing, our financial security?

Did I become a mother the day we hit ‘viability week’ and breathed a small sigh of relief, while knowing nothing is guaranteed? 

Was it the moment we sat on the cliff edge at sunset, whittling down our shortlist until we picked the boys’ names and said them aloud into the canyon?

Am I a mother now, when I look down and can’t see my toes, when rolling over in bed takes all my effort, when I don’t have the energy to sit upright at my desk, when my blood nose drips all over the serviettes at the restaurant, when I pee a little every time I sneeze, when I start to feel more like a vessel than a woman?

Am I a mother yet? 

A mother before they’re here? 

Does motherhood come upon me the moment the first of my babies enters the world and I feel their skin on mine, and hear their cries?

No. 

Because I’ve known so many women who never got to hold their baby in their arms and, even still, all of them — mothers.

I’m a mother, too.

Today marks three months with our “mini boys” (as dubbed by one of their little cousins haha). 

Becoming parents has been slow, chaotic, gentle, busy, difficult, natural, and a complete unfolding of ourselves, and all those things cancel each other out until it’s just you and your babies and blearily whispered “I love you”s at ungodly hours.

I thought I’d feel cooped-up; I feel free. 

I thought I’d feel anxious; I feel at peace.

I thought I’d feel left out; I feel content.

I thought I’d feel overwhelmed; I feel capable.

DXxNByVTjtQ.content:
Asking for help is hard; it’s something I’ve never been good at, and a muscle I’m having to exercise more and more these days since becoming a mum.

Recently Matt was away for a few days, and a few of you asked how I went about asking for help in that time— I thought I’d share what I did here for anyone who wants to get better at it with me 🫶🏼

1. I made a list of people who’ve offered to help in the past. I tried to think of the people I’d feel the most comfortable coming into my home and being with the boys.

2. I added those people into a group chat. I did this for two reasons; firstly, it meant that no one person felt like they HAD to help or that all the pressure was on them alone; they could see they were part of a bigger group effort, and secondly, it just simplified the organising of it all.

3. The hardest bit was to brainstorm *exactly* what I needed while Matt was away, so that instead of just vaguely asking for help, I could communicate really clearly HOW people could help. (I ended up saying “I would love someone to come over and help me with our dinner, bath & bedtime routine from 5:30-7pm.”)

4. I then gave everyone in the group chat a few different options (literally in a poll), so they could pick and choose what suited their schedule & capacity.

5. Finally, I made it really clear that I would really appreciate the help, but tried to also give an out (e.g. “I’d be so grateful for an extra pair of hands, but I completely understand if you aren’t able to this weekend!”). I didn’t want to downplay how much the help was needed, but I also wanted them to know I’d survive if no one was available — it’s a tricky balance to strike haha.

I’ve been learning that so many people want to help but just don’t know what to offer, so it’s really up to us to be able to communicate exactly what we need!

I hope some of this encourages you to be bold in asking for the help you need, and in learning to accept it when it’s offered, too 💛

#firsttimemum #firsttimemom #twinmum #twinmom

DX5LMV8T_ba.content:
It’s a Monday morning and your husband is running late for work. 

Toys are strewn all over the house, the sink is full, and banana is smooshed into the carpet. 

Your hair is unbrushed, you’re still rubbing your eyes from sleep, and you’re trying to scoff down some toast before the babies notice.

There’s a chorus of tears, a vomit incident (onto the tiles, thank goodness), snotty noses dribbling down past chins, and it’s not even 8am.

But then… this. 

They crawl to the open door and watch their daddy walk out, put on his jacket and helmet, and sit patiently as they wait for their favourite part.

He starts up the engine, rolls the bike forward, raises a gloved hand and waves. 

You watch their little faces smile in recognition—that’s DADDY—and he gives them a grin and a moment to take it in before putting off to work.

It’s quiet after he drives off, them still processing his absence, and you think somehow, strangely, in your messy house with your messy hair and your sticky babies—

—you are the luckiest girl in the entire world.

DYJG_q1q_kU.content:
I’m sitting in a dark room, two pudgy cheeks pressed into my stomach, marvelling at how these tiny bodies—not so tiny anymore, really—used to fit inside of me. 

On this day last year, 20 weeks pregnant, I hadn’t yet felt their kicks and now, somehow, their wobbly little legs are standing and climbing and their brains are learning faster than I ever thought possible. They’re just like me, really; still the same people that existed last year, and yet transformed into something entirely new. 

I didn’t think becoming a mum would change me for the better. Quite honestly, I thought I’d become some lesser version of myself; fractured, frazzled, run down & afraid, poor on time and desperately lonely. And though I’ve felt snippets of all of those things since their early arrival 9 months ago, I’ve found that, unquestionably, these boys have changed me for the better. 

My head carries more than it ever did before, and yet I’m learning to slow down; to focus on moments; to find joy in the in between. My friendships have shifted, but rather than dwindled, they’ve multiplied, stretched, and deepened. 

I’m quicker to laugh, to go with the flow, and to show grace. I’m less anxious, which is truly a miracle for someone who’s grown up with an active imagination and a jittery brain, and although there’s no performance review or pay check for this role, I feel more fulfilled than I ever have before.

Today, my first Mother’s Day as a mum, I’m so grateful for everyone who has helped me on this journey to motherhood; my mum, who has shaped who I am; my mother-and-sisters-in-law, who’ve shown me beautiful versions of motherhood, my family and friends, new and old, who’ve cried and laughed and made meals and sat with me, and Matt, who makes me want to have lots more babies so the world can have more people like him (only slightly kidding). 

And finally, I’m grateful to Reuben and Judah, who I somehow miss even while I’m holding them — thank you for helping me grow.

Have you ever thought about the importance of setting boundaries for your mental health? Establishing healthy boundaries can be a game changer in your personal and professional life. They help you create a clear distinction between your needs and the demands of others, allowing you to prioritize your well-being.

Consider this: when you say "yes" to every request, you might feel overwhelmed and unable to focus on what truly matters to you. Setting boundaries empowers you to communicate your limits effectively, which can reduce stress and enhance your relationships. It’s not selfish; it’s a necessary practice for maintaining mental clarity and emotional balance.

Start small. Identify one area in your life where you feel stretched too thin and practice saying "no" or setting a limit. How do you feel afterward? The more you practice, the easier it becomes to establish boundaries in other aspects of your life.

Remember, boundaries are essential for fostering a healthy relationship with yourself and others. How do you prioritize your mental health through boundary setting? Share your thoughts and experiences in the comments below.

“Why ‘be more strict’ made everything worse with ADHD…”

“Be more consistent.”

“Be stricter.”

“Set clearer consequences.”

I heard this so often as a mother.

But with ADHD (and especially neurodivergent children), constant pressure and escalation often lead to *more overwhelm*, not understanding.

When the nervous system is already dysregulated, consequences in that moment rarely create learning — they usually increase stress on both sides. 💔

What actually helps is what comes *after* the moment:

calm co-regulation, reconnecting, and gently replaying situations without pressure.

Not to shame.

Not to punish.

But to build understanding. 🤍

You don’t need to become harsher.

You need tools that work with the nervous system, not against it.

DVBLhkNgRUI.content:
🌿🤎 Things To Say To Soothe Your Inner Child 🤎

Inner child healing is about reconnecting with the younger version of you — the part that still carries old wounds, unmet needs, and unspoken emotions. 🧸✨

When we experience trauma, neglect, rejection, or emotional pain in childhood, those experiences don’t just disappear. They live quietly inside us — shaping our relationships 💔, self-worth 💭, boundaries 🚧, and even the way we speak to ourselves.

Inner child work is the process of gently saying:
“I see you.” 👀
“I hear you.” 👂
“You matter.” ❤️

It’s about re-parenting yourself with compassion instead of criticism. 🌱
It’s about replacing shame with understanding. 🕊️
It’s about choosing self-love over self-blame. 💞

When you practice inner child healing, you may begin to:
✨ Build healthier relationships
✨ Improve emotional regulation
✨ Increase self-confidence
✨ Release childhood trauma
✨ Strengthen boundaries
✨ Feel safer in your own body

Healing doesn’t mean pretending the past didn’t happen.
It means giving yourself what you didn’t receive back then. 🤍

You deserve safety.
You deserve love.
You deserve gentleness.

If this resonates, save this post 💾
Share it with someone who needs it 💌
And speak kindly to yourself today 🫶

🌐

❤️💔😞❤️‍🩹
A lot of men born in the late 80s and early 90s were raised by emotionally disconnected examples of manhood. Pride. Ego. “Man up.” No vulnerability. No emotional healing. No God.

Some of us had fathers in the house, some didn’t, but never had true male figures leading us.

Now men in their late 30s and mid to late 40s are trying to break cycles while fighting trauma, pressure, anxiety, anger, failed communication, marriage struggles, and emotional damage we never learned how to process.

At the same time, we’re raising kids in a world consumed by social media, clout, pornography, comparison, depression, and zero real guidance.

That’s why so many young boys are lost.

This is a generational snowball effect.

Most boys don’t need more followers. They need fathers. Mentors. Godly men willing to lead them the right way.

I’m praying for all the silent fathers, brothers, and husbands carrying this weight every day.

This is not your fault. It’s a cultural curse many of us inherited and now have to remap through God, healing, accountability, and truth.

If this is you, know you are loved. Jesus died for your sins so you could have eternal life if you repent and believe.

You do not have to become what you saw growing up.

#MenOfGod #BreakTheCycle #FatherhoodMatters #MentalHealthAwareness #JesusSaves

C4G4elSyVSQ.content:
I want to live life on slow motion 🫶

So I asked chat GPT HOW TO DO SO. Here is an answer 

Mindfulness: Practice being fully present in the moment. Notice the details of your surroundings, the sensations in your body, and your thoughts and feelings without judgment.

Slowing Down: Intentionally slow down your pace. Walk slower, eat slower, and give yourself more time to complete tasks.

Enjoy Simple Pleasures: Notice and appreciate the little things that bring you joy, like a cup of tea, a beautiful sunset, or a good book.

Disconnect: Take breaks from technology and social media. Instead, engage in activities that allow you to be fully present.

Prioritize: Focus on what truly matters to you and let go of things that don’t align with your values or goals.

Nature: Spend time in nature. Nature has a way of slowing us down and helping us feel more connected to the world around us.

Limit Distractions: Identify and reduce sources of distraction in your life, whether it’s clutter, noise, or too many commitments.

Practice Gratitude: Regularly take time to appreciate the good things in your life. This can help you feel more content and present.

Learn to say No: Don’t overcommit yourself. Saying no to things that don’t align with your priorities can help you slow down and focus on what’s important.

Breathe: Deep breathing can help you relax and feel more grounded. Take a few moments throughout the day to focus on your breath.

DYsoqIPv0dj.content:
For a long time I thought maybe I was “too independent.”

You hear it all the time, especially as a woman.

“You’re intimidating.”
“You don’t need anyone.”
“You’ve built your own life, you are too much in  your own strength… maybe you struggle to let people in.”

And I sat with that.

Because I don’t actually feel anxious when I’m not in control. I can go with the flow. I can trust. I can laugh when things don’t go to plan.

But when it comes to the really big things — marriage, children, building a life with someone — something shifts.

Not because I need to control every outcome.

But because some decisions aren’t small.

You’re not choosing a dinner spot. You’re choosing who sees you at your lowest. Who raises your children. Who shapes the atmosphere in your home. Who stands beside you in grief, stress, growth and the ordinary days in between.

Maybe some of us aren’t “hyper-independent.”

Maybe we just know what it feels like to carry heavy things alone.

Maybe we know what it feels like to be disappointed, to rebuild, to start over, to become our own safety net.

And when you’ve spent years building yourself back up, you become careful with what — and who — you hand your future to.

There’s a difference between not needing anyone and wanting to choose wisely.

I’m curious…

What’s one thing you became “too much of” because life asked you to be?

Too independent? Too strong? Too guarded? Too understanding?

I’ll read every one 🤍

CdlRm_KsQfV.content:
How is it with our kids, they get on a scale and we are happy at their weight? But with ourselves, we are fearful, holding our breath and filling ourselves with anxiety? 

It is because of how we think. 

With our kids, It means they are growing… it is confirmation that we are not completely failing at this parenting thing. 
Even when a child is overweight or underweight, we don’t think like a failure. We think “what does our child need next?” 

But with us, we somehow think that the scale means we are a failure. We think the number is telling us we are ugly, not good enough, unworthy of accomplishing our dreams. 

Here is a new thought. 
The number is just a number. It tells us what is working or what isn’t working. What did you do differently the day before to be down a pound? What did you do to go up a pound? 

When we start thinking with curiosity, let go of the expectations of anything our weight, we can then finally move forward with love, respect, and grace day by day with our weights numerical number. 

#newthought

Cd_mnjqrv-L.content:
Habit

Habit is the hardest thing to change. If you are used to eating popcorn at the movies, eat snacks in front of the tv, needing to get dessert… if you have been doing this for years, it is habit by now. It takes you needing to constantly ask yourself “am I hungry?” 

Emotion

We have a toxic, emotional relationship with food. There is first off healthy food, unhealthy food, there is okay food, sweet cheating food. There is indulging food… how about this. 

Throw all of those old negative fearful, hurtful thoughts about food out and just think… “food is food” it is nourishment for when you are hungry. It will help lead you to how you want to feel after being hungry, which is satisfied. 

Culture

Our culture is embedded with unhealthy food thoughts. They want you to eat their food at a restaurant because it gives them money. They make nothing off you having a glass of water. 

Bakeries display their food to make you think about eating. Cinnabon makes fresh cinnamon rolls to make you want to eat it. 

Our culture says bigger is better and have a “lunch deal” 2 for 5. 

Remember, before you indulge, ask yourself, “am I hungry?”

#mindfuleating #weightlosstips 

We live in a world we’re we are being sold anything and everything. There are even books on how to breathe right. Something that is supposed to be so simply focused so simple needs instruction. The same thing has happened in weight loss. We need “professional” advice and plans to get us the results that we want. But that isn’t true. 

We don’t need anymore plans, anymore diets. No more counting. No more restriction. The goal is to learn to trust the self. We don’t. We apparently need to trust everyone else but ourselves. 

As I write my book I wonder when the end point will be because it seems we are driven to a point where we always need to rely on the words of everyone to simply function. 

There is an end to the endless desire to humans. My goal is to stop the consumerism and bring the world to balance.

DVJuY1HkvVc.content:
This is my pantry. I’ve had many pantry more past and now as I clean this pantry up to prepare me for the next few months, I’m reminded of what it used to look like. Foods that just expired never got eaten, one time only foods that made no sense to my diet… 

And now that I’m responsible for five lives total, my pantry is more organized than when I was single. When I was single, it was a mess and made no sense. Now as I re-organize and put things in the spot that I like, I am amazed of how little I needed to really throw away in this process. If you look at the things that we eat on a regular basis, you’ll see that they’re not always “healthy“ because mindful eating isn’t about healthy foods. It’s about eating foods that feel your body and add value to your life.

Do we like to eat, healthy? Absolutely! But you’ll see more of those foods in my refrigerator. The only thing I’m debating about getting rid of is the Ragu tomato sauce. I actually didn’t buy that somebody from my Instacart delivered it to me with my other order but I feel weird about throwing it away right now. Maybe I could use it in a dish for my small group or use it to make food for a family that needs help.

Fruit Bowl Choc Muffins 

These are delicious!
Makes 6 large muffins

2 over ripe bananas
1 over ripe pear
2 eggs
30 grams extra virgin olive oil
25 grams milk
100 grams wholemeal self raising flower
3 tablespoons chia seeds
1 tsp bicarb
2 tablespoons coco powder
60 grams dark chocolate buttons for after the blending process

Separate the eggs and beat the egg whites to firm peaks.
Add all ingredients to a blender/thermo and blend until smooth.
Stir in dark chocolate buttons.
Spoon into miffun pan
Bake for 10 mins on 200 degrees, reduce to 160 degree and cook until cooked through, approx 15mins

DL9rRupzDll.content:
Chicken lasagne 🐔 
No bari swaps here tonight, but a great alternative to white sauce is 1 egg beaten with 500 grams ricotta

6 Fresh lasagne sheets
Mixed mushrooms sliced 3 cups uncooked
Shredded bbq chicken 
1 diced onion
2 garlic cloves crushed 
1 large bag of baby spinach or box of frozen
Dried thyme and oregano
1 teaspoon stock paste 
40grams plain flour
500ml milk
40grams butter

Saute onion and garlic in olive oil and add mushrooms, cook until tender.
Add shredded bbq chicken, spinach, stock, dash of water, and herbs and cook until spinach is wiltered.
I make my white saue using the bechamel recipe in the TM6. Alternatively, in a saucepan, make a roux using butter and flour and gradually add milk, season with salt.
Layer lasagne sheets, chicken mix, and white sauce until baking dish is full. Top with white sauce and cheese and bake for 30 mins.

Beef Strog 

4 pack of coles quick cook scotch steak thinly sliced
3 cups uncooked sliced mushrooms
1 onion Diced
2 garlic cloves crushed
2 tablespoons white wine
1 tspn thyme
1 tspn Thermo chicken stock paste
1 tablespoon Worcestershire

200 grams lite sour cream 

Pan fry steak, onion, and garlic in a hot fry pan quickly to sear meat.
Set aside.
Add mushrooms to a pan with some butter and fry.
Add wine and thyme and cook off.
Add stock, Worcestershire, tomato paste, and sour cream. Return steak and onion mix to pan.
Stir to combine.
I serve mine with aldi imperial borwn rice and quinoa, but thinly sliced steamed cabbage is such a good pairing or ribboned zucchini lengths.

Simple Fried Rice 
Makes 5 bari serves
218 calories l 25.9g carbs l 9.4g fat l 6.7g protein

1 packet coles microwave brown rice
2 eggs
1 rash of bacon
1 celery stalk finely Diced
1 garlic clove
Half carrot grated
2 tablespoons sesame oil 
2 tablespoons of soy or Tamari 
*I also regularly swap out the rice for cauliflower and add on spring onions + capsicum

Heat brown to packet instructions 
Whisk 2 eggs in a bowl
In an electric fry pan heat 1/2 of the sesame oil to a high temperature and add egg. I like to pick the pan up and allow the egg mix to spread to all sides which rapidly fries it. It should take 30-60 seconds.
Fold cooked egg in half and remove from pan and cut into strips.
Add remaining seasmae oil and finely dice bacon to fry pan with crushed garlic
Add prepared veggies and fry off
Add heated brown rice and fry for 2 mins
Add egg back in and tamari or soy sauce 

Always served with wings 😍 these are aldi maple bbq wings

BsWaPV6gI8A.content: 18 weeks and 4 days with Joey and 18 weeks and 4 days with Baby Never Going To Have A Name Because We Can’t Decide. I remember taking that photo with Joey. I had been in bed all day as per my life at that point and I thought I should probably take a photo now that I was “putting on weight”. In reality I was still quite under my start weight. This time I was prepared for the joys of HG. Our goal was to put on 10kg before conception. I got to 7.5 which I was happy with. However - I only lost 3kg during the first trimester this time so a BIG improvement - and also a bigger belly and rounder hips, softer arms etc! 😂 But I think any #hyperemesisgravidarum mum would agree - I will take putting on weight in pregnancy a million times over compared to losing it!! THIS is our reality right now.

Everyone bathed in an oatmeal and coconut oil bath (including mummy IN the bath lol) and in pyjamas and I was very proud of that!

But - there was no time for me to put pants on before Joey wanted to love her brother a little *too* much.

Snuggled up tired to the bone, reading books waiting for Daddy to quickly eat his dinner so he can take Noah while I have Mummy and Joey time at the end of a long day when she doesn’t get much Mummy time at all

Noah has done some all night sleeps recently and I’ve been SO happy I’ve posted about them in my stories.

But that’s also not the full story.

Please know that we have also had over ten appointments in the last 3 weeks because of lactose overload, lip, tongue and buckle ties, breastmilk oversupply as well as intolerances and all of the issues that come with all of those things combined.

I slept sitting up like I was on an airplane holding Noah for OVER 3 weeks straight because he needed to be vertical because he was in so much pain. 
My neck felt like I was 80 years old.

I called my mum in tears to come and help one morning at 4am because the walls in our bedroom appeared to me to be bending and moving and it wasn’t safe for me to hold Noah.

We seem to be over the “hump” of that now and things are getting much easier thank goodness.

But just thought I’d post in case anyone needs a reminder that what you see on social media is what people WANT you to see. It’s the highlights reel. 
It’s real, sure, to some extent, but it’s never the whole story.

While the photo on the left will be up on display in my house forever, I never want to forget the photo on the right when my babies were so small and needed me so much 🥰 #behindthenewbornphotoshoot

Thank you @hannah.dahlen for sharing this. 

That last sentence hits hard. No change in mortality rates. No. Change. 

These interventions are not “saving lives”. They’re creating real, life altering, sometimes debilitating trauma. And for what?

Less than half of the humans born in this country now aren’t born physiologically the way humans were designed to do. If that doesn’t blow your mind and make you concerned for the future generations to come, you and I are very different people! 

What is the flow on effect? Think birth is individual and so there isn’t one? Did you know some scientists have hypothesised that if we follow on on this tragectory,  through evolution in just a few short decades humans won’t be able to give birth at all without surgery?! That’s not okay. That will never be okay! Birth doesn’t have to look like this!! It should never have gotten to this point! Birth can be incredible. Women have incredible births every day all around the world!!

Mumma’s now more than ever it is up to YOU to become informed and do absolutely everything you possibly can to prepare mentally, emotionally and physically for birth - data doesn’t lie. You have GOT to take full responsibility if you want to do all you can to minimise the true trauma risk.

Find the women who have had the experiences you want to have and ask them everything. I promise you - women who have had beautiful births want to share. We WANT to spread the word “Hey! Birth can be amazing!! Let me show you what helped me!!” 

This is what put me on the path from one of the most traumatic birth stories I know to now being a total birth junkie - I knew someone who had had the experience I wanted to have, I asked her what she did to achieve that, I listened - and then I got to work (forever grateful for @groundedbeginnings_ )

These stats do not have to include you! But (there will obviously always be true medical exceptions) that’s honestly up to you. Birth is a marathon and you have got to put the training in.
