“Never take advice from someone you wouldn’t trade places with.” That’s it. That’s the quote I try to live my life by. 

How cool is it that you can just hear something one day that resonates so deeply with you & then decide to live your life by it.

Whether it’s in motherhood, relationships, health, finances, work, lifestyle - anything. If they aren’t living a life I would be happy to look back on & claim as my own, I’m taking their advice with a grain of salt. If they don’t have what I want - WHY would I listen to them?

& care for them - but haven’t achieved what they really want in the first place.

I seek out people who have what I want. I model them. Your journey is yours alone. It doesn’t have to make sense to everyone currently around you. I want to thank everyone who has reached out, cooked meals, donated, sent flowers, cleaned our home, and packed away the baby things so gently. Zac - Mummy loves you more than words are capable of even expressing. Like I promised you, I WILL find you, please wait for me: My soul knows your soul baby and I WILL find you xx

You grieve for your baby - but as a mother, you grieve a different loss all over again for each of your surviving children too. I don’t know yet how I’m going to show up for them to be the mother they deserve… I just know that at some point, I have to.

DP-KMl4AWdV.content:
October is both Pregnancy & Infant Loss Awareness Month and Down Syndrome Awareness Month - and today marks four weeks since Zac died.

Zac had Down syndrome. We didn’t know before he was born. Every scan was “normal.” I’ve checked - and so has the team at Mater, one of the best in the country. Not even one soft marker. Even the scan minutes before he was born - nothing.

I wish so badly we knew. He would have been classed as high-risk and monitored more closely & maybe had a chance. I never knew that sometimes - extremely rare, incredibly “unlucky” & “almost unheard of” - there can be no signs at all.

Did you know the NIPT test can sometimes miss it, and that some babies show no visible signs on any scans at all? Me either. I’m not trying to spread fear - I just didn’t know. I think most people don’t.

What I’ve learned since is that the extra chromosome can affect everything - including the placenta and umbilical cord - sometimes making them fragile in ways you can’t see. That’s meant to bring comfort the professionals tell me - to hear “there’s nothing anyone could have done with the information we had” - but it doesn’t. It just brings heartbreak. It just seems so unfair.

They say understanding “why” is meant to help. But all I feel is pain, because I wish I could have known sooner. I would have done anything to save him.

There are quite a few potential risks associated with Down syndrome pregnancies - not just heart issues like I once thought - & if known, those pregnancies should be watched closely. Sometimes babies need to come a little earlier or need extra support.

I share Zac’s story not to create fear, but to share his truth - and how deeply he was loved. His siblings adored him. I would have devoted my whole life to him. He would have been idolised in our family. I just wish we knew.

Zac, my beautiful boy - I think of you in every breath, every heartbeat, every minute of every day. I miss you SO much. I’m sorry I’m not showing up the way I promised. Mummy just needs more time. 🧡

Even at Tacos & Tequila, my soul is getting downloads…

They always let us dance.

They had to.

Because even in the most controlled systems, even under the heaviest expectations, they knew we needed something to stay human.

So they let us sweat on the floor, bend our backs, swing our hips, drop it low.

Because dancing is soul expression wrapped in rhythm.

But listen…

While they let us dance, they locked up the other doors to soul alignment:

Stillness.

Sensuality.

Real, raw love.

Pleasure and joy.

Ancestral connection.

Communal care.

Slowness as power.

Deep conversation.

Saying “nah” to what don’t fit.

Saying “YES” to what only we know is medicine.

While we should ABSOLUTELY dance.

We also need ask to as ourselves :

When was the last time I felt this free outside the club?

If you don’t have an answer… there’s work to be done between the beats.

Because your soul doesn’t just need rhythm.

She needs you. All of you.

In the light. In the quiet. In the whole life you were born to live.

There’s still ongoing conversation about whether the City will end the Comprehensive Plan contract — but here’s what we really need to pay attention to:

The Comprehensive Plan is our city’s land use plan. 
It’s our opportunity to shape how land is used in our neighborhoods for the next 20 years. And if we don’t speak up now, decisions will be made for us… again.

Land use determines everything: 🏫 where our schools sit 🥕 whether we have access to grocery stores 🚶🏽‍♀️ safe walking paths 🌳 green spaces ♿️ disability access 🏠 and whether development actually includes the people who already live here

City Council recently voted against requiring affordable housing in future development and has also voted recently voted to close many Pgh area schools. 

If we don’t show up now and put forward clear recommendations in the Comp Plan, we will see more of the same.

If we want sustainable, community-centered growth, the Comprehensive Plan must continue — and our voices must be in it.

DYzWqh6HxYu.content:
A couple questions for y’all…

Did you get time off work after having your first baby? Your second? Your third?

Did you get time off after losing someone you deeply loved?

If you experienced a disability, whether it was temporary like a broken leg or something you still navigate today, did you get the time and support you needed to adjust to your new reality?

If the answer is no, it’s because Allegheny County still does not have mandatory paid leave protections for workers.

But we have a chance to change that.

On June 2nd at 5:30 PM, there will be a public hearing at the Allegheny County Courthouse regarding mandatory paid leave. Then on June 16th, Allegheny County Council will receive a proposal to either pass or deny 18 weeks of mandatory paid leave in Allegheny County.

Brown Mamas and I will be there advocating for families, caregivers, workers, and everyday people who deserve time to heal, grieve, recover, and care for themselves and their loved ones without risking their livelihood.

We would truly love your support and presence.

Because rest, recovery, caregiving, and healing should not be luxuries.

DDkpIQsz-QF.content:
The fourth morning in a row I've woken at 5am to the unmistakable combo of glossy black cockatoo screeches and the sound of cones dropping on our timber decking.

These birds are a listed threatened species and their population is still declining. The pressures they face include the felling of very old and tall trees (they need large hollows which take hundreds of years to form). There's also pretty fierce competition for these hollows between sulphur crested cockatoos, corellas, galahs and the introduced common myna. 

Glossy's are also very selective feeders and rely heavily on she-oaks like this one as their primary food source. She-oaks have a complex relationship with fire, and although many species are somewhat dependent on fire for regeneration, others are highly fire-sensitive and do not survive severe fires, something which is becoming increasingly common with climate change. It was well documented that there was a significant reduction in foraging habitat availability post the megafires of 2019-2020. 

These beautiful birds are very long-lived and they mate for life, only producing one chick every two years. This pair produced their chick last year 🥹 I'm utterly enamored by this species and I'm so grateful each morning that I get to see them. Given they seem to love the cones from this particular tree, if anybody in SEQ or FNE NSW would like some seeds to plant on your property, please DM me. 🫶🏼 

#glossyblackcockatoo #conservation #endangeredspecies

DJbtZ5IybxK.content:
Hydration 💧 + Breastfeeding 🍼 = 🤝

Everyone knows of the importance of staying hydrated while breastfeeding, but here's a breakdown of WHY its so important 💖

My Ashkenazi ancestors fled before the Holocaust. Those who didn’t were made martyrs.
I don’t know why G-d allows tragedies like the Shoa to happen. It’s one of life’s big unanswered questions:
Why did G-d harden Paroh’s heart?
Why did the Shoa happen?
Why did October 7th happen?

And so on.

What I do know is that we have a choice in how we respond to tragedy. I’m not separate from those who were lost. None of us are.

I find it particularly striking that Ashkenazim share the same 300 ancestors. We multiplied into millions… and we were nearly wiped out.

But our soul is eternal.

I don’t know why I belong to a family that survived pogroms. Why they got out of Europe faster than others. But I do know that by deepening my love for my fellow Jew, and by trying to make the world— even just my own little world— as good as I can, I hope to honor the memory of the 6 million we lost.

Never forget.
Never forgive.
Never again is now, every day.

#neveragain #neveragainisnow #yomhashoa #amyisraelchai

Text: 
You in LA? 
Yup. Why you want a hug? 
Yes. 
I texted Steve before hopping on the 101 west. Heading to the beach to roller skate.  Lately hot essential oil bubble baths and exercise are my go to therapy. I have a lot on my mind. It’s Holy weekend and I’m honestly hoping to resurrect the feeling of true love in life. 

Steve started pursuing me back in 2005. I was working as a phlebotomist in Gardena, Ca. One year before graduating nursing school at Mount St. Mary’s college. Almost three years ago he found me through Facebook’s “people you may know “ feature. 
He say that he never stopped thinking about me. Hearing that is nothing new, I have a trail of broken hearts. 
Steve is originally from Detroit. Brown skin complexion, tall with a naturally muscular build. Easygoing brother. Flips houses in Los Angeles. 

We met up at Randy’s donuts in Inglewood.  He looking a hot mess. We break the ice by talking about current events. 
“Where’s your mask?” I ask 
“I don’t need one.” he replied. He recently lost his mom to the novel coronavirus. His dad recovered. Steve says “I could see the devil in each breath my dad took. That’s why I got vaccinated.  You vaccinated? 

“No. That sounds like a horrible experience, Steve. I’m glad pops recovered. I’m sorry about the loss of your mom. “
Steve looks at me intently waiting for me to acknowledge him. He always have looked me deeply in my eyes, like he has something special just for me. 
“Glennae, you don’t have faith in men. A dude will tell you just who he is. You got to be listening.” 
“Yea. That’s true. I do be listening. “
“No. No you don’t. You like these niggas who blow smoke up your ass. Then feed you shit. That guy, you’ll give him all your thoughts, all your  time and you still single.” 

I close my eyes, turn my head rejecting his opinion and take a breath “Ok thanks for pulling up! I’m going now” I reply 

“There you go, track star! Always running. Call me later knuckle head.” He said. 

I know exactly why I do this! 
Stems from childhood. Healing myself.

My peace has never been the same. 

Ladies, some lessons we can do without. Have you ever been in a situation ship that you knew was going the wrong way?

Omista kipukohdista on hyvä olla riittävän tietoinen, mutta…

Tarua. Auttajan ei tarvitse olla täydellinen. Joitakin vuosia sitten tätä kysymystä pohtiessani silloinen psykoterapeuttini sanoi viisaasti, että myös auttaja saa olla vasta ”matkalla”. 

Auttajan ei tarvitse olla malli jostakin, joksi asiakkaan tulisi tulla tai muuttua.

Sen sijaan meidän tehtävä on edes auttaa sellaisen tilan syntymistä, jossa asiakas voi löytää ITSE ITSENSÄ: 

”Tavallinen uutta kehitysobjektia koskeva väärinymmärrys on se, että on kyse psykoterapeutin/auttajan itsensä tarjoamisesta, ikään kuin mallina, jonka mukaan potilas/asiakas alkaisi sitten muovautua. Tosiasiassa on kyse objektista, jonka avulla potilas/asiakas voi löytää oman itsen potentiaalin.” (Riitta Tähkä - Löytää ja tulla löydetyksi)

Suomeksi sanottuna auttajan ei tarvitse olla itse mikään malliesimerkki tai kansankynttilä. Pelkkä ihminen riittää. Auttamistyössä on tärkeä pyrkiä luomaan sellaiset olosuhteet että asiakas voi löytää itse itsensä ja voimavaransa.

Mentalisaatioteorian mukaan keskeinen syy sille, miksi toinen traumatisoituu vaikean tapahtuman jälkeen ja toinen ei ➡️ johtuu siitä, että traumaoireita lopulta saava on vaikean tapahtuman jälkeen jäänyt ilman muiden ihmisten tukea ja turvaa. 

Vaikean tilanteen jälkeen tarvitsemme aina toisten ihmisten mieliä ja säätelyapua käsitelläksemme tapahtunutta niin ajatusten kuin tunteiden tasolla. 

Ikävä kyllä sellaistakin on tullut työssä vastaan, että ihminen on kohdannut vaikeaa kaltoinkohtelua ja kukaan läheinen ei ole koskaan palannut asiaan ja ollut kiinnostunut kannattelemaan tapahtunutta yhdessä. Meillä ihmisillä tai ainakin suomalaisilla on taipumus vältellä vaikeita asioita, joten tämänkaltaiset ilmiöt lienee aika yleisiä. 

Mikäli tukea (eli toisia ihmisiä ja heidän mieliään käsittelyn apuna) ei ole saatavilla, keskeinen seuraava tunne yksin jäämisestä on häpeä. 

Häpeän tunne taas yrittää saada meidät vetäytymään edelleen lisää, joten kierre on valmis. 

Eli ➡️ sinun tai jonkun muun traumaoireet EIVÄT johdu siitä että olisit/hän olisi jotenkin keskimääräistä heikompi tyyppi. 

Keskeinen juttu on yleensä se, mitä tapahtuu vaikean tapahtuman JÄLKEEN suhteessa muihin ihmisiin. Resilienssi ei ole yksityinen on/off ominaisuus vaan se rakentuu vuorovaikutuksessa.

‼️ Ps. mitä näihin epämentalisoivien moodien nimiin tulee niin mentalisaatioterapian yksi kehittäjä Anthony Batemankin totesi niiden olevan ”shitty names” 🫠 Bateman kutsuu pretend modea ”bubbleksi” koska tässä moodissa ihminen saattaa elää kuin omassa kuplassaan, yksin ‼️

Pretend mode ei kuitenkaan siis todellakaan ole tietoista teeskentelyä vaan se on eräänlainen automaattinen tapa olla (ja selviytyä). Usein pretend modessa on kyse siitä, että ihminen katkaisee yhteyden omiin aitoihin kokemuksiin, tunteisiin ja tarpeisiin. Tällöin voi tuntua ettei tunne itseään, on hukannut itsensä tai valehtelee itselleen.

Arkinen esimerkki on se, että sinusta saattaa tuntua ettei asiat omassa elämässä ole ihan niin kuin pitäisi mutta hoet itsellesi kaiken olevan hyvin tai sinulla on jopa eräänlainen ”hällä väliä” olotila jossa mikään ei oikein tunnu miltään. Toisaalta taas saatat ”pakottaa” itsesi positiiviseksi ja reippaaksi tukahduttaen samalla muita aitoja kokemuksiasi (tämä on tosi tavallista).

Usein tämä näkyy myös vuorovaikutuksessa siten, että aidot kokemuksesi eivät välity muille ja olo voi olla eristynyt, ulkopuolinen, ei-ymmärretty. Pretend mode on tuttu pärjääjätyypeille jotka piilottavat oman haavoittuvuutensa sen taa ja samalla jäävät kokemustasolla yksin. 

Vakavampi esimerkki on dissosiaatio, joka on olotilana sellainen että tunteet on eristetty omasta tietoisuudesta täysin.

C8HeGKcthey.content:
Mentalisaatiosta eli mielen supervoimasta.

Luonnon meille luoma kyky mentalisointiin herätellään lapsuuden riittävän hyvissä kiintymyssuhteissa, yleensä suhteessa äitiin ja tänä päivänä onneksi myös suhteessa isiin. Mentalisointi tarkoittaa kykyä tarkastella sekää omaa mieltä että muiden mieliä. 

Riittävä mentalisointi takaa kasvavalle ihmiselle kyvyn mm. tunteiden säätelyyn, leikkiin, sosiaalisten suhteiden solmimiseen, oppimiseen sekä yleiseen luottamukseen elämää kohtaan. Varmasti jokainen haluaa tuuppia omaa lastaan kohti näitä 🧡

Miten muun muassa annat lapsellesi eväitä mentalisaation kehitykseen? 

🧡 Ole kiinnostunut ja utelias siitä mitä lapsen mielessä liikkuu
🧡 Kohtele lasta aina yksilöllisenä ja ainutlaatuisena tyyppinä
🧡 Peilaa lapsen tunnetiloja siten, että siinä on lapsen ilmaiseman tunteen lisäksi samalla säätelevä ja tarvittaessa rauhoitteleva sävy (esim. kun vastaat hätään lohduttavasti etkä omalla hädälläsi)
🧡 Sanoita omia ajatuksiasi ja tunteitasi lapselle ikäsopivasti, malliintaaksesi omaa mieltäsi ja sen ainutlaatuisuutta
🧡 Ollessasi lapsen kanssa ylivireä tai hankalan tunteen äärellä, ota aikalisä/hengähdyshetki ja toimi/sano vasta sitten (jos se on enää edes tarpeen)

Aika perusjuttuja? 🧡 

Kuvitteleppa sitten itsesi kuormittuneeseen, kiireiseen ja vaikeiden tunteiden vallassa olevaan tilaan. Näissä hetkissä mielen jousto vähenee (mutta älä huoli - nekin hetket on osa elämää)

Nämä hetket on kuitenkin niitä, jolloin me tarvitaan eniten tietoa mentalisaatiosta ja tietoista itsen palauttamista mentalisoivaan tilaan. Yleensä mentalisoivaan tilaan meitä palauttaa jo sen huomaaminen, mitä itsessä tapahtuu.

Jos haluat kuulla lisää tästä mielen taidosta jää kuulolle 🧡🧡🧡 

Tällä tilillä jaan yleistä tietoa mentalisaatiosta eli mielen joustavuudesta.

Ikävä kyllä auttajan omat kokemukset eivät kuitenkaan takaa sitä, että asiakas tulisi jotenkin paremmin ja empaattisemmin autetuksi.

Omat kokemukset, varsinkin riittämättömällä tavalla käsitellyt, saattavat tuoda työskentelyyn itse asiassa vuorovaikutukseen haitallisella tavalla vaikuttavia ilmiöitä, esimerkiksi auttajan tiedostamattomia vastatunteita.

Pahimmillaan näiden pohjalta sitten lähdetään neuvomaan tai ohjeistamaan asiakasta mustavalkoisesti, reagoidaan asiakkaaseen jotenkin ei-suotuisalla tavalla tai auttaja ei yksinkertaisesti pysy joustavassa mentalisoinnin tilassa vaan uppoaa esim. omiin vaikeisiin tunteisiinsa tai kokemuksiinsa. 

En sano etteikö omia vaikeita kokemuksia saisi olla ja useimmilla meistä on. Näyttöä siihen suuntaan, että siitä olisi työlle joka tilanteessa apua saatika että sen varaan kannattaisi kokonaan auttajan ammattinsa ja työnsä perustaa ei kuitenkaan ole.

🧡 Parempi itsetuntemus ja myönteisempi ajattelu itsestä

C8ZuqV8IxyN.content:
”Transferenssi on pysähtynyt, itseään toistava näytelmä, jossa on lukkoon lyödyt psyykkiset sisällöt” (Riitta Tähkä kirjassa Löytää ja tulla löydetyksi).

Transferenssia voi ajatella myös ”väärinä tunteita väärässä paikassa, vääriin henkilöihin kohdistettuina” (Muurinen, 2011).

Elikkä suomeksi ➡️ Auttamissuhteeseen tulee aina mukana myös menneisyys (sekä asiakkaan että auttajan). Yleisimmin transferenssilla kuitenkin tarkoitetaan sitä, että asiakas saattaa odottaa/nähdä/kuulla/kokea auttajassaan ja heidän välisessä suhteessaan jotain, joka on tuttua hänen menneisyytensä ihmissuhteista, eikä niinkään ajankohtaisesta auttamissuhteesta (tämä ei tarkoita etteikö auttajallakin olisi oma roolinsa siinä millaiseksi suhde muodostuu). Varsin usein nämä olettamukset ovat kielteisiä.

Mikäli näitä ilmiöitä ei oteta puheeksi on vaarana yllä olevassa sitaatissa kuvattu itseään toistava näytelmä, josta klassinen esimerkki on vaikkapa asiakas joka pettyy auttajiinsa toistuvasti ja pahimmillaan siirtyy ammattilaiselta toiselle kykenemättä luomaan syvempää suhdetta. 

Puheeksi ottaminen ja ylipäätään transferenssin huomaaminen on tietysti auttajan vastuulla. Moderni näkökulma on se, että itse asiassa transferenssista voi olla myös suurta hyötyä, kaikkine riskeineen. Transferenssia puretaan korjaavilla kokemuksilla, eli sillä, että auttaja toimiikin parhaansa mukaan toisin kuin asiakkaan menneisyyden näytelmä olettaa.

Jos haluat oppia lisää siitä mitä auttamistyössä tapahtuu rivien välissä (tää on yleensä juuri se mistä me tässä työssä kuormitutaan!) niin tule mukaan elokuun koulutukseen Astetta syvempää auttamistyötä 27.8.2024 🧡 Opit lisäksi auttajan vastatunteista ja vuorovaikutuksen katkoksista. C8o751btdmk.content:
Psykoanalyyttisen teoreetikon Wilfred Bionin mukaan psykoterapian tavoite on asiakkaan kyky kärsiä. 

Kuulostaako oudolta tai pessimistiseltä? 

Kyvyn kärsiä voi ajatella kuitenkin myös:
🩵 kykynä olla yhteydessä omiin aitoihin tunteisiin ja sietää ne 
🩵 kykynä surra se, mitä on menettänyt tai ei koskaan saanut (esim. turvallinen lapsuus)
🩵 kykynä kokea tervettä vihaa sitä kohtaan, mikä ei ole ollut oikein tai reilua
🩵 kykynä tunnistaa myös se, mistä itse olemme vastuussa
🩵 kykynä olla haavoittuvainen

Ilman kykyä kärsiä olemme jumissa erilaisten oireiden kuten ahdistuneisuuden kanssa. Toimimme itselle haitalliseen tapaan kuten suoritamme tai ohitamme omat aidot tunteet ja tarpeet. Samalla saatamme pitää muut tunnetasolla ja psyykkisesti ikään kuin ”käden mitan päässä” (ja olemme ehkä vältteleviä). 

Mentalisaation näkökulmasta olemme ehkä ei-mentalisoivassa moodissa nimeltä pretend mode, joka voi tuntua siltä, että elää omassa ei-aidossa kuplassa jossa ei ole mitään tuntemisen arvoista, syytä surulle tai vihalle saatika tarkemmalle tutkimiselle. Pretend mode kieltää kärsimyksen ja omat kohtaamattomat tarpeet: ”what’s done is done”, ”menneitä ei voi muuttaa joten miksi niitä miettisi” tai ”mitä hyötyä on surkuttelusta”. 

Kyvyn kärsiä sivutuotteena on kuitenkin erilaiset sävyt kärsimyksen rinnalle kuten toiveikkuus, rauhallisempi sisäinen olo ja myötätunto. Kokonaan kärsimys ei kuitenkaan koskaan poistu koska se on osa aitoa elämää.

C8rk2H9tZOX.content:
Millainen on mentalisoiva auttaja? 

Aloitetaan sillä, mitä ei kannata tehdä.

😰 Älä yritä tehdä hienoja ja syvällisiä tulkintoja asiakkaasta
😰 Älä tarjoa monimutkaisia interventioita tai harjoitteita
😰 Älä mene mukaan pretend modeen, jossa vuorovaikutus on näennäisen toimivaa mutta jää pinnalliseksi ja ei-aidoksi (muista että terapian tavoite on kyky kärsiä❗️)
😰 Älä oleta, että tiedät mitä asiakkaan mielessä liikkuu
😰 Älä esitä näkökulmiasi totuutena
😰 Älä keskity vain siihen MITÄ puhutaan vaan myös siihen MITEN puhutaan, teidän välillä, tässä ja nyt
😰 Älä tee oletuksia asiakkaasta tai käytä transferenssi-näkökulmaa siten, että oletat asiakkaan käytöksen johtuvan vain jostain menneisyyden tapahtumasta ja sillä siisti (ilman että sinulla vuorovaikutuskumppanina olisi vaikutusta asiaan)
😰 Älä ole hiljaa pitkiä aikoja
😰 Älä reagoi tai vastaa asiakkaalle jostain omasta intensiivisestä tunnetilasta käsin, vaikka tunteet on siis auttajallekin täysin sallittuja (ne täytyy vaan tuoda ilmi säädellyssä muodossa, kuten vanhempi tuo parhaimmillaan lapselle)

Nämä vinkit perustuu mentalisaatioterapian brittiläisten kehittäjien teksteihin, jotka on siinä mielessä hauskoja että he uskaltavat antaa tällaisia konkreetteja ”do’s and dont’s” -listoja 👌🏼 Myös huumori on tärkeä osa mentalisoivaa terapiaa ja asennetta. 

Muista myös, että mentalisoiva asenne ei ole staattinen, pysyvä tai lopullisesti saavutettu olotila auttajallakaan vaan me kaikki löydämme itsemme aika ajoin yllä olevasta listasta. Ei olla siis armottomia itsellemme.

Olet varmaan kuullut tän joskus itsekin ja oh boy että tämä tyyli ajatella on tiukassa, terveydenhuoltoa myöten. Tällä usein myös perustellaan kaikenlaista olettavaa, epäasiallistakin painopuhetta ja painostigmojen ylläpitoa.

Mistä tässä ajattelutavassa oikein on psykologisesti kyse?

Yksi taitavan ja joustavan ajattelun eli mentalisaation pulmista näyttäytyy juuri tällaisena mustavalkoisena, yksioikoisena tyylinä ajatella, jossa mielen sisäiset päätelmät tapahtuu pelkästään nähtävissä olevien ilmiöiden ja fyysisen todellisuuden varassa ➡️ ”hoikkuus ja normaalipaino ovat merkkejä terveydestä joten ylipainoinen ei voi olla terve”

❗️mentalisaatioteoriass nimeltään tämä on teleologista ajattelua (suomeksi esim. liikaa ulkoiseen maailmaan nojaava kokemistapa)❗️

Esimerkkejä tämänkaltaisista mentalisoinnin haasteista laajemmin muissa tilanteissa: puolisoni ei välitä minusta koska ei sano sitä usein tai terapeuttini ei pidä minusta koska ei vastaa viestiini heti. Oletetaan siis, ettei asia voi olla totta, koska ”ei näytä siltä” tai että asia on tavalla x koska näyttää siltä. 

Onnistunutta mentalisointia taas olisi ajatella, että….
✨ en voi ulkonäön tai painon perusteella tehdä päätelmiä ihmisen terveydestä
✨ vaikka ylipainolla voi olla keskimääräinen yhteys eri terveysriskeihin se ei tarkoita sitä, että juuri tällä edessäni olevalla ihmisellä olisi jokin sairaus tai välttämättä edes riskiä sille (keskiarvot eivät kerro totuutta yksittäisistä ihmisistä, ethän oleta jokaisen kohtaamasi mieheksi identifioituvankaan tekevän vähän kotitöitä vaan koska miehet niin keskimääräisesti tekevät, vai?)
✨ terveys ja hyvinvointi on monimutkainen kokonaisuus ja ennen kaikkea ”more than meets the eye”

Ajattelun joustavuutta eli mentalisaatiota on onneksi mahdollista kehittää 🧡 Omalla tililläni kerron mentalisaatiosta eri näkökulmista. Hyppää seuraamaan jos mentalisointi mielen taitona kiinnostaa ✨

Auttamistyössä me pyrimme korjaaviin kokemuksiin. 

Korjaava kokemus tarkoittaa sitä, että auttamissuhteessa mahdollistuu jotain uutta, hyvää ja korjaavaa, jota vaille asiakas on aiemmin elämässään (tai lapsuudessaan) jäänyt, esim:

🧡 tunne että minusta ollaan kiinnostuneita
🧡 voin osoittaa vaikeita tunteita ja olla silti turvassa
🧡 väärinkäsitykset eivät katkaise suhdetta

Korjaava kokemus ei kuitenkan ole jotain, joka asiakkaalle vain TUOTETAAN ja hän sen passiivisesti ottaa vastaan. Tämä näkemys aliarvioi asiakkaan. 

Asiakkaan täytyy olla tässä prosessissa itsekin aktiivinen toimija, joka:

🧡 on riittävän avoin
🧡 rohkaistuu tutkimaan itseään ja omia reaktioita

Mentalisaatio on mielen supervoima, koska sen avulla pystymme asettumaan sekä kanssaihmisten henkisiin saappaisiin että tutustumaan itseemme syvemmin. 

Toimiva mentalisaatio tarkoittaa sitä, että voimme kuvitella muiden mielen liikkeitä ja samalla havainnoida mitä itsessämme tapahtuu.

Mutta joskus tämäkin menee överiksi.

Tätä kutsutaan hypermentalisoinniksi.

Hypermentalisoija on tottunut olettamaan liikaa muiden ajatuksia ja tunteita. Samalla hän saattaa ottaa oletuksensa liian todesta, eikä muista kyseenalaistaa niitä. 

Esimerkki: kaveri vastaa viestiin viiveellä ja hypementalisoiva oletus on, että syy on jokin vanha väärinymmärrys välillämme eikä hän oikeasti edes tahdo olla tekemisissä kanssani. 

Super yleinen hypermentalisoinnin merkki onkin tulkinnat hylätyksi tulosta.

Mikä avuksi? 

🧡 Kysy itseltäsi: Tiedänkö tämän todella? 
🧡 Mitä minä itse koen ja tarvitsen? Käännä huomio toisten mielten analysoinnista kohti itseäsi.

DEm-BhWt1U8.content:
Myötätuntouupumus on auttamisaloilla melko mukisematta hyväksytty termi mutta se on oikeestaan käsitteenä niin laaja että puhuessamme siitä me saatetaan puhua ihan eri asioista.

Mun näkemys on se, ettei myötätunto uuvuta. Ennemminkin aidon empatian ja myötätunnon tunteminen voimauttaa ja saa jaksamaan työssä. 

Tämän sanominen ääneen herättää usein vastareaktioita tyyliin ”kylläpäs uuvuttaa ja sillä sipuli” ja en aina ihan ymmärrä miksi. Liittyykö siihen oletus ettei saisi olla töistään uupunut?

Se ei ole ollenkaan mun pointti. Tottakai saa ja monet on. Itsekin olen ollut. Jotta voi auttaa itseään on kuitenkin tärkeä ymmärtää mistä oma uupumus koostuu. Sen sijaan että toteaisi että ”tää työ nyt vaan on tällaista” ja ”se on se myötuntouupumus” - halki poikki pinoon, ilman sen kummempaa pureskelua…

Varsinaisia syitä uupumukselle liiallisen myötunnon sijaan voi olla:
🔸 Koet, että ”vain annat ja annat” etkä saa koskaan takaisin (yleensä tällöin sinun omat toiveet ja tarpeet ei ole tulleet riittävästi täytetyiksi ja tämä voi juontaa myös henkilökohtaisen elämän puolelta)
🔸 Otat asiakkaiden asiat liiaksi omille harteillesi, kadotat terveet rajat tai vaadit itseltäsi mahdottomia
🔸 Sinulla on ollut liikaa työtä tai et ole voinut tehdä työtä arvojesi mukaisesti
🔸 Itse asiassa saatat kamppailla myötätunnon puutteen ja kyynisyyden kanssa (ehkä seurausta yllä olevista?)
🔸 Koet ettet pysty vaikuttamaan omaan työhösi tai asiakkaiden asioihin
🔸 Koet työssäsi riittämättömyyttä joka kumpuaa esim. siitä että aidosti työskentelet jatkuvasti osaamistasosi ylärajoilla TAI riittämättömyyden tunne on henkilökohtainen ydinkipusi

Ps. Sitten samalla tähän teemaan liittyen tulee tosi komppaavia kommentteja missä tunnistetaan mitä haen takaa. Jännä ilmiö!

Pps. mun kanssa saa siis olla eri mieltä 😌

Jos olet kiinnostunut pureskelemaan enemmän sitä, mikä auttamistyössä oikein uuvuttaa niin olet erittäin tervetullut linjoille 28.1.2025 Auttajan Jaksaminen -työpajaan 🔥🔥 ET SAA ”nuku paremmin” ja ”ajattele vähemmän töitä” -vinkkejä vaan ihan jotain muuta 💫

DEzuANztfQs.content:
Tämänkaltainen keskustelu asiakkaan kanssa (tässä tietysti typistettynä versiona):

Asiakas: ”Kuormittaakohan minun asiat sinua ja miten ylipäätään jaksat tätä työtä?”

Minä (hämmästyneenä asiakkaan huolesta): ”Itse asiassa mä pidän työstäni enkä koe että kuormittaisit minua” 🧡

Läsnä oli siis klassinen transferenssi eli se, että asiakas kokee minun kanssa jotain samaa mitä muissa ihmissuhteissaan. Että muut ei jaksa häntä tai hänen täytyy suojella muita ja olla vahva. Transferenssit ei siis vaadi sitä, että kyseessä on pitkä terapia vaan erilaiset olettamukset vuorovaikutuksesta herää jo lyhyissä kontakteissa, usein jo ensitapaamisella.

Mutta miksi tuo keskustelu oli päivän ellei viikon paras juttu?

Siksi, että pystyin sanomaan 100% rehellisesti ja sydämestä, että pidän työstäni enkä koe olevani asiakastyöstä erityisen kuormittunut.

Voi kuulostaa itsestäänselvyydeltä mutta sitä se ei todellakaan ole esimerkiksi kuormittuneena, ei ole ollut omallakaan kohdallani. Omakin polku on sisältänyt kaikenlaisia vaiheita ja lyhytkestoisen uupumuksenkin. Olen tuntenut riittämättömyyttä, liiallista vastuuta työstäni, sitä kuinka vastaanottojen jälkeen on ihan uupunut tai ylivireä, sitä etten osaa auttaa jne… Ja välillä tunnen noita inhimillisiä tuntemuksia edelleen eikä tässäkään asiassa tarvitse tulla valmiiksi.

Jos haluat kuulla minun näkökulmia siihen mikä auttamistyössä saa jaksamaan pitkällä tähtäimellä, tule mukaan 28.1.2025 Auttajan Jaksaminen -työpajaan.

Työpajassa esim:
🔸mikä meitä kuormittaa?
🔸 auttamisen halua vai myös jotain muuta? - tunne omat motiivisi auttamistyössä
🔸 vastatunteet työhyvinvoinnin tukena
🔸 mentalisaatiotuntemus ja mentalisoiva työote
🔸 näkökulmia auttajan rajoihin
🔸 saat ajatuksia herätteleviä tehtäviä
🔸 asetutaan olemaan, tunnistellaan omia tarpeita ja rentoudutaan hetkeksi

DE2U0iztBal.content:
Tämä on esimerkki, jonka annan usein ja johon myös törmää usein.

Tiedäätkö sen tunteen asiakkaan kanssa kun tuntuu, että pitäisi tehdä ENEMMÄN ja PAREMMIN, antaa neuvoja tai jotain ”kättä pitempää”. Olo on riittämätön. Asiakas saattaa osoittaa tyytymättömyyttään tai sit tää on enemmän tunnelma, joka ei tule sanoitetuksi.

Tottakai voi olla kyse siitä että teidän yhteistyössä on tullut kupruja tai ettet ole saanut ihan kiinni siitä mitä asiakas toivoo tai mikä häntä auttaisi.

Joskus tuo riittämättömyys on kuitenkin vastatunne, joka kumpuaa siitä että asiakas ei mentalisoi ja on esimentaalisessa teleologisessa moodissa. Tuossa moodissa ”vain teot ratkaisee” ja mielen tiloille pitää pääsääntöisesti pyrkiä tekemään jotain. Asiat pitää ratkaista. Se että kuulosteltaisiin omia ajatuksia ja tunteita ja siedettäisiin ne, on teleologiselle moodille ihan hepreaa. Ja kaikkihan me joskus päädytään tohon tilaan, esim. kun tuntuu siltä ettei paskaa fiilistä paranna mikään muu kuin tekeminen, vaikkapa hikilenkki tai siivoaminen tai tunnesyöminen.

Auttajalle kyseinen moodi voi kuitenkin aiheuttaa yllä olevia ahtaita oloja. Kirjaimellisesti tunnet olevasi ahtaalla ja koet, että nyt pitää KEKSIÄ jotain tai ottaa käyttöön jokin hieno menetelmä tai kotitehtävä.

Kun huomaat kyseistä ahtautta sen sijaan että yrittäisit tehdä enemmän ja premmin voisitko itse asiassa kuulostella vastatunnettasi ja sitä, onko teleologinen moodi läsnä? 

Jos haluat kuulla lisää, tule 28.1.2025 Auttajan Jaksaminen -työpajaan 🔥🧡💫 Siellä vastatunteita ja kaikkea muuta 🧡

Sinä ja sinun tekemiset asiakkaiden kanssa ei ehkä ole ihan niin tärkeää kuin luulet. Voit siis huokaista helpotuksesta.

60-70% asiakkaiden myönteisestä muutoksesta liittyykin itse asiassa asiakkaaseen itseensä ja esim näihin seikkoihin:

“The trials of today will not last forever. God is turning your pain into purpose and your struggles into testimonies.”
Romans 8:18

Today, Me & @__screambri WAKE UP call was deeper than normal and I admitted some real shit — it’s the middle of December, the year is wrapping up, the holidays are here… and I am not exactly where I thought I’d be. Life didn’t go according to “My timeline”. Some days feel heavier than others, and the pressure of “being strong” wears on me in ways most people don’t always see. Because I’ve been told I handle it  so well.

But even in the uncertainty, God keeps showing us that we’re not walking alone. We show up for each other as friends. We show up for our families. We show up for our daughters. We show up even when we’re tired, even when we’re confused, even when the journey doesn’t make sense yet.

And that’s the beauty of it — showing up is still progress. Showing up is still faith. Showing up is still growth.

So if you’re ending this year feeling like you’re behind, like you should’ve accomplished more, or like life hit harder than expected… breathe. God is still writing your story. What feels like pressure today is preparing you for something bigger tomorrow. Your “not yet” is not a “no” — it’s a setup for a testimony that will make sense in hindsight.

Here’s to grace, friendship, and the quiet strength that keeps us going. And here’s to walking into the next season with expectation, not fear. God’s not done. 🤍✨ #Miami #winterinmiami #friends #adultfriendships #girlsgirl

Acceptance - Surrender 
SURRENDER is another word for leting go. It's looking at something and seeing what's missing, but loving it as it is, with the absent pieces. It's taking a leap forward, not because I know it is safe but because I trust that it will be, somehow. And I know the future holds a light I cannot see but is worth every fear I have to face in order to get there.

Heal - Loneliness 
LONELINESS is the last petal on a rose, the last leaf on the tree. It's believing I don't belong and staying here, in the middle, hoping someone will take me. It's not seeing the thread of light between you and me because I am too heartbroken and no one taught me that love is there even when I cannot feel.

Release - Attachment 
ATTACHMENT is rooted in the fear of losing everything I dare to love. It's merging with a feeling to the point of losing touch with my true identity. My things and I are bound so tightly that I cannot tell them from me. My pain and I are bound even tighter: losing it would be losing me.

Where's my crunchy mamas at! 🙌🏻🙌🏻🙌🏻

Here's a list of things that we do, as first time parents, that tend to shock many others! My son's infant care teachers even thought that I'm in the early childhood educating industry too! 

✨ Babywearing 
✨ Bedsharing
✨ Elimination Communication 
✨ Cloth Diapering 
✨ Using & Teaching ASL (sign language)
✨ Baking Homemade Sourdough 
✨ No Swaddles, Mittens & Socks
✨ No Oats & Porridge

I never believed that first time mamas are inexperienced. 

I never believe that it takes more than the first child to know how to parent. 

Many of these listed above are not even what second time parents do. And yet how do I know about it? It stems from my parenting philosophy and beliefs. Coupled with collecting knowledge and going along with my intuition, this is why we do the things we do. 

 
Not saying I'm doing the best, but we're definitely confident even as first time parents.

DQoSAywkQ_G.content:
✨ Turning a haircut into a mini art studio 🎨✂️

As a mama with a little bit of a perfectionist streak in me, I started the haircut high hopes of having it done perfectly.

But my little explorer had other ideas. He wiggled, shouted “No!”, and turned the dining table into his own art canvas.

Things shifted when we handed him his favorite markers. Suddenly, the haircut became a play time with his markers.

He drew lines and circles, laughed, and had fun. It turned a stressful moment into shared joy.

What I learned:
💫 Mess is magic — A little chaos can unlock the biggest smiles.
💫 Give them agency — When kids co-create, they engage with more joy and less resistance.
💫 Celebrate the process — Messy is the default mode. Joy is the choice in the middle of it.
💫 Reward after — It’s not about the flawless haircut. It’s about showing up even through perfectionism & anxiety.

So next time you’re in a wiggle-war, grab the markers, splash some water, and let the bubbles fly.

The mess fades, but the laughter stays. 💛
How do you manage situations like this? 💭

DRgVEDakQFt.content:
I’ve been sitting with this for a longggfg time… 
and tbh, I don’t resonate with the label “first-time mother.”

Yes — this is my first child.
And yes — this was technically my second pregnancy.
But the assumption that “first-time” equals naïve or inexperienced… that part doesn’t land well with me.

By the time I conceived & was in my pregnancy, I had already read deeply, listened intentionally, asked better questions, and chosen the kind of village that would shape me into the mother I wanted to be.

Not because I wanted to be perfect.
But because I am committed to breaking cycles.
Because I want my child to receive what I didn’t.
Because I believe motherhood begins long before birth.

And I want to say this gently, but clearly:

Please don’t place yourself beneath anyone just because this is your first pregnancy or your first time mothering.

You’re not “less than” because your journey is beginning.
You don’t owe automatic authority to people simply because they’ve done it before.

With the right community, knowledge, and internal grounding, you can make choices that feel deeply aligned for you — and stand by them, even in front of medical professionals, elders, or strangers with loud opinions.

Motherhood is not measured by the number of pregnancies.
It’s shaped by intention, awareness, and the willingness to lead yourself.

Trust yourself.
Your voice is allowed to matter from the very beginning.

💖 Join me in my telegram space

Do you celebrate your lunar birthday?

Growing up, my grandma always cooked mian xian with a duck leg for our lunar birthdays.

No candles. 
No cake. 
Just a warm bowl of soup noodles 

Now that I’ve moved out, life doesn’t always line up with our Saturday visits.
So instead, she gives me ang bao money and tells me to buy my own roasted duck leg.
so the tradition continues.

It’s not so much about the food.
It’s about remembrance, continuity, and care passed quietly through generations.

What makes me smile is how my husband takes this seriously too.
Last night, we ate out,  just to get that duck leg.

And it got me thinking…
Traditions don’t have to be big or perfect.
They just have to be felt.

What’s one tradition you hope your children will remember,  or one which you want to start?

DYeoFoemgG_.content:
People think financial planning is about numbers. 🔢
It never was.

At 21, I was sitting across clients talking about money —
but what I was really holding were deep conversations about fear, what ifs, and relationships. 🤝

I learned to notice the pause before someone answered.
The change in tone when a topic felt uncomfortable.
What was said.
And what wasn’t.

I didn’t know it then, but I was building up towards coaching. ✨

Today, watching a group of children quietly observe a classmate having a meltdown, I recognised the same thing happening. 👀

No one told them what to do.
They were simply watching.
Learning.
Sensing.

The ability to observe without rushing in.
To notice before speaking.
To understand before advising.

That skill has been with me long before I ever called myself a coach. 🌿

And it’s still how I work today.

Maybe you are like many employees across the nation.

You went to the doctor with a body full of symptoms.

Headaches.
Fatigue.
Trouble sleeping.
High blood pressure.
Anxiety.
Muscle tension.
Brain fog.
Crying spells.
Dread before work.

And you felt dismissed.

Then a short time later, a preventable stress-related disease appeared and you thought:

“I knew something was wrong. That doctor gaslit me.”

But here is another possibility:

The doctor may not have ignored you.

The disease may not have fully manifested yet.

Doctors are positioned for disease management, diagnosis, and treatment.

But chronic job stress often shows up before disease becomes diagnosable.

That is the window most workers miss.

And when chronic job stress lasts longer than six weeks without proper assessment, your body may keep adapting until adaptation becomes disease.

So the question becomes:

Did the doctor miss you?

Or did the system never teach you that work fatigue requires its own assessment before disease shows up?

That is why Workforce Care™ exists.

We try to catch Black career women and RNs the moment they say:

“I need a break.”

Because that moment matters.

Before you resign.
Before you accept a label.
Before you enter disability.
Before you return to the same environment with no strategy.
Before stress becomes disease.

We help you assess what your body may already be telling you.

Take the Work Fatigue Quiz™.

Catch the stress before it becomes the disease.

DYaitSBksZI.content:
Work fatigue is not one thing.

That is why so many workers misread it.

You may think you are just tired.

But chronic job stress can show up in different ways:

Mental fatigue — brain fog, overthinking, forgetfulness, decision fatigue.

Emotional fatigue — crying spells, irritability, dread, numbness, anger.

Ethical fatigue — feeling forced to work against your values, silence your concerns, or participate in unsafe conditions.

Physical fatigue — headaches, high blood pressure, muscle pain, insomnia, GI issues, exhaustion.

Spiritual fatigue — feeling disconnected from purpose, calling, faith, identity, or the person you used to be.

This is why the Work Fatigue Quiz™ matters.

It helps identify the level of work fatigue you may be experiencing so you can stop guessing and start moving in the right direction.

Because burnout is not always sudden.

Sometimes it is the result of ignored signals, unassessed stress, and staying too long in an environment your body has been warning you about.

You do not need to wait until your body breaks down to take your work stress seriously.

Before burnout, there is work fatigue.

Take the Work Fatigue Quiz™.

Know your level.
Name what is happening.
Move in the right direction before burnout makes the decision for you.

Workforce Care™ is a nurse-led support model for Black career women and nurses dealing with workplace stress, burnout, and workforce instability.

We assess your symptoms and work environment to help you navigate leave, recovery, and return-to-work decisions more safely.

Are you a therapist or psychiatrist?

No.

I am an RN specializing in Workforce Care™ and workforce recovery support.

I help clients understand their experiences, navigate systems, and make informed workplace health decisions.

Do you accept insurance?

No. Workforce Care™ is a private-pay service.

Are you accepting new clients?

Yes.

Why don’t you accept insurance?

Because I work exclusively for YOU.

Workforce Care™ provides workforce-centered guidance and recovery support without many traditional system limitations.

What is the Work Fatigue Quiz™?

The Work Fatigue Quiz™ is a free nurse-led assessment that helps identify work fatigue before burnout worsens.

What happens after I take the quiz?

You may receive:

a workforce-centered assessment

practical guidance and education

insight into workplace stress patterns

next-step recommendations

Who is Workforce Care™ for?

Workforce Care™ was created for:

Black career women

nurses and healthcare workers

high-functioning professionals

employees experiencing workplace stress or burnout

What kinds of concerns do clients commonly experience?

Clients often report:

workplace stress

emotional exhaustion

burnout

moral distress

fear about employability

confusion about FMLA, ADA, or disability systems

physical and emotional overwhelm

Are your assessments free?

Yes. Current assessments are free.

Simply comment “Fatigue” or request the Work Fatigue Quiz™ through the provided link.

Are there fees for services?

Yes. Workforce Care™ services are self-pay.

Many clients consider the support and guidance a worthwhile investment.

Why does Workforce Care™ matter?

Because protecting your ability to:

function safely

think clearly

make informed decisions

navigate systems

remain in the workforce

matters.

DYpXmaVv8SQ.content:
Work Fatigue™ is chronic job stress that has begun affecting the worker mentally, emotionally, physically, ethically, or spiritually.

This week, we read from Operation Mental Health: Practical Lessons on Career Burnout and Recovery and held live lessons on:

My Doctor Approved My Leave… So Why Was My STD Denied?

FMLA Approved. ADA Requested. Now HR Is Acting Different.

What Happens When Work Is the Reason You’re Breaking Down?

Your Anxiety May Be Real… But Is the Job the Root Cause?

The Hardest Part About FMLA? Deciding What to Say.

Next week, I’ll be going Live on Facebook with:

“Many Workers Are Afraid to Tell the Truth About Their Job.”

And they are.

Many workers are breaking down under chronic job stress, unsafe conditions, discrimination, retaliation, moral distress, and systems they were never taught how to navigate.

Some are approved for leave but still confused.

Some are seeing doctors but still not getting answers.

Some are talking to HR but now feel watched.

Some are wondering if they are depressed, anxious, burned out, or simply exhausted from telling the truth in a system that benefits from their silence.

That is why Workforce Care™ exists.

Not to replace medicine.
Not to replace legal advice.
Not to tell you what to do.

But to help you assess what is happening, understand the systems you may be entering, and make informed employee health decisions before burnout deepens.

If your job stress has lasted longer than 6 weeks, do not keep guessing.

Take the Work Fatigue Quiz™.

Success leaves clues. If you knew what I have been through, what I survived, and what I still chose to build, your head would spin.

Obedience to Yahweh, following the way, the truth, and the life — that is how I made it through.

And I will say this with love:

If you are seeking help for work-related suffering and no one is helping you tell the truth, protect your dignity, understand your options, or return to the way of Christ, pay attention.

Everything that sounds helpful is not the right way.

I love you.

Take the Work Fatigue Quiz™ today. #nurses #fmla #glennaesrxforlife #healthcare

DYqt5nHvaqY.content:
Heyyyy 😂 this video is from my 2019 photo shoot. I had a lot of fun, and I’m glad this impromptu interview happened because I really do not share much about myself.

Truthfully, I’m reserved. My work has always been about YOU, the people of God.

But if you’re a little nosey and truly want to know who I am, what I survived, and how this work came to be… I wrote two books. Grab your copy.

As a founder, visionary, practicing RN, and menopausal Black woman, I’m already doing entirely too much 😂

My head has been down building ever since I was fired for disability as a practicing RN. In 2015

And before then, during that season, and even now, the enemy has continually tried to distract me. Sometimes he did.

Now listen… a 6’3 dark-skinned brother from The Town almost had me out here missing destiny entirely 😩😂

If I can be honest, there were moments I truly thought the assignment had been taken away from me.

Nevertheless, I am closer now to the vision God gave me back in 2007, and at this point nothing can stop what was ordained.

Next week, I’ll continue reading Operation Mental Health and giving real-time, real-world lessons to help you cope better and not lose your mind, money, health, talent, or gifts navigating these workplaces with BIG audacity.

Let’s humble them.

Before burnout… there’s work fatigue.

DY0c8Yaj8EL.content:
We offer peri-FMLA Workforce Care™ services ensuring Black career women and RNs are never left alone to fend for themselves.

By the time you finally take FMLA, you have already been through the most. You are already hurt, exhausted, overwhelmed, emotionally drained, and unsure what to do next.

What you may not realize is that FMLA is often only the entry point.

You may also be entering:
• HR
• Disability
• ADA
• Psychiatry
• Return-to-work negotiations

Nobody warns you the system is connected and often defending itself.

Let a professional RN specializing in workplace mental health, systems navigation, and workforce recovery provide the direction, assessment, and protection you deserve before entering the system alone. If job stress lasts longer than 6 weeks. Take our Work Fatigue Quiz. Ask me what the benefits are for you.

Lately, life has felt unbearably heavy a path I never imagined I’d walk, one that only those who’ve lived it can truly understand.
This journey tests every part of me my body, my heart, my spirit. It breaks me and builds me, all at once.

I hate feeling helpless.
I hate the ache of watching others hold what I’ve been dreaming of for so long.
I tell myself to stay strong, to keep believing,
to trust that I am braver than the pain that keeps finding me.

Some days, I manage.
Other days, I fall quite lost in the silence of what could have been. Even surrounded by love and support, there’s an emptiness only I can feel.

So I move gently, one day at a time,
carrying hope in trembling hands,
trying to make peace with the ache that lives beneath my ribs the ache of wanting, waiting, and still believing.

Important update for every bus rider in Harlem — this is changing later in 2026.⁠
⁠
MTA buses will no longer accept coins as fare payment.⁠
⁠
If you currently pay with coins, here is what you need to know:⁠
⁠
Your options going forward:⁠
— Tap your phone⁠
— Tap a contactless debit or credit card⁠
— Use an OMNY Card⁠
⁠
No smartphone or bank card? No problem.⁠
You can load an OMNY Card with cash — paper money or coins — at OMNY vending machines in subway stations or at stores near you like Walgreens and CVS.⁠
⁠
And here is something worth knowing: if you pay for 12 trips with the same card or device within 7 days, the rest of your trips that week are free. That is the OMNY fare-capping benefit — and it saves you money.⁠
⁠
Senator Cleare wants every rider in Harlem to be ready for this change before it happens. Share this with your family and neighbors.⁠
⁠
For more info: mta.info/omny⁠
⁠

DYXsylODShk.content:
NYC's rent freeze program for seniors and disabled New Yorkers hasn't been updated in 20 years.⁠
⁠
SCRIE and DRIE — the Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption and Disability Rent Increase Exemption — are two of the most powerful tools New York has to keep seniors and people with disabilities in their homes. These programs freeze your rent and protect you from future increases. But the income eligibility limit hasn't changed since the early 2000s. Thousands of New Yorkers who should qualify no longer do — because the number never kept up with reality.⁠
⁠
Senator Cleare stood with her legislative partners in Albany this week to demand that these bills come to the floor. As Chair of the Senate Aging Committee, she put it plainly:⁠
⁠
"Imagine waiting 20 years for a raise."⁠
⁠
Seniors and disabled New Yorkers deserve to age in place — with dignity, stability, and a rent they can actually afford. This bill needs to pass this year.⁠
⁠
If you or someone you know may qualify for SCRIE or DRIE, visit nyc.gov/rentfreeze or call 311.⁠
⁠

CIX2CPtn7f9.content:
Reflection 
How do you even manage time?? 

I'm always stressed out in Sweden, I have a lot of people I care for and I never seem to spend enough time with any of them. I have this year left it a bit out of my hands and spent most time with whomever asks for me. Not making too many plans for myself but accept any invitation. Trying to squeeze out as much as possible out of every hour. This have completely left myself out of the equation which in turn has left me stressed out. Always thinking, it's fine I will have time for myself when I get back home. My morning routine gone, meditation gone, exercise gone, down time gone. Well this will be the damn last time.🤦‍♀️I'm still learning to put myself first, and with my weak ass body I know I need to make some healthy habits that stay in routine in order for me to function well. 
I'm not waiting for new years to make this promise to myself but I might hold off just another 2 weeks 🙄😆💜

Cl3o5fQDwch.content:
My baby is 10 months old.
She can drink from a glass, she can take 18 steps all on her own. She winks at me. She loves being chased around. She copies everything we do and noises we make. She can say 3 words but sticks to mama. 

She is the most precious little creature I ever saw. 

Every little hardship that's been, is nothing really.
Birth, breastfeeding, crying, back aches, head aches. It all fades with one look at her.

Everytime she cries a bit too much, I remind myself that it's a hard time being 10 months old and not being able to communicate your wants and needs. But more than that I remind myself that I'm freaking grateful of her existence, and that her crying, whining and wanting to be glued to me, is a part of it. I pick her up and take a second to soak in the moment. To really feel her body against mine. The size of her, her weight in my arms, the smell of her. The way she lean her head against my shoulder. 
I might need my two hands for whatever I'm doing but you know what? I'll make do with one because this is my baby. My Precious little darling girl who wants me to hold her. And I enjoy every bit of it because I know I will wake up one day and she won't ask me to hold her no more. And there will be another day when I won't even be able to. 
There is beauty in that progress too but it also kind of sucks. 
So she can nurse, she can whinge until i have her in my arms again. 
I can sigh and very occasionally find it inconvenient. But it's okay. Because it's temporary. I'll hold her, and I'll cherish it even when I'm dead tired. 
She is already double digits. She is almost a whole year. 

even tho I remind myself daily to soak her in, to enjoy the moment, to cherish her and be grateful for all the good and the less good, time slips through my fingers and memories too. She grows and is a whole new baby every month. I can't believe how little she was just 5 months ago. It feels like yesterday. 

I shed a little tear because I will never hold that little baby in that shape or form again. And I pull my now 10 month old a little closer, hug her tight and remember that she will never be this little again. 
 
! Note; i wrote this almost 4 weeks ago now 😥

C3l4G8HP4AD.content:
For this deeeelicious recipe you will need; 

600g chicken thigh meat
2 TBS olive oil
4 cloves of garlic diced or minced
Brown Onion (optional)
3/4 cup cherry tomatoes 
2 tsp Italian seasoning
1/2 tsp salt
1 cup risoni
2 1/2 cups chicken broth
270ml can of coconut milk (I use Ayam brand) or you could use thickened cream
2 large handfuls of spinach
3/4 cup Parmesan cheese

Cut your chicken thigh into cubes, add olive oil to the frying pan (medium-high heat) and cook the chicken for 3 mins (doesn’t need to be completely cooked at this stage just have the majority of it turn white). Add garlic (you could add a diced brown onion at this stage too if you like), Italian seasoning and salt, cook this for another 4 minutes, add the risoni, chicken stock stir well and let it cook for about 12-15 mins with a lid on, stirring a few times. Once the risoni is cooked, add in that coconut milk, stir and cook for another minute before adding your spinach. Cook that for another minute, then finally add the paresan cheese, stir through and cook for another final minute. I then leave mine for 5-10 mins with the heat off. Serve and enjoy! This serves 4 adult servings with an additional 2 meals for my twins. Zara hasn’t tried this yet, her words were ‘it looks like it might be nice but I think it would be gross for me’. Give her time, she’ll try it and love it I’m sure. 

Originally I got this recipe from @kalejunkie who has faaaabulous recipes! This one she calls her ‘marry me chicken orzo’ (orzo = risoni).

Kids on an elimination diet; in our case it needs to be done but man it just feels cruel.

Eczema has become SO bad the past 6 months and I wasn’t willing to just keep putting steroid cream on it for it to go away but then flare up again a week later. I knew enough to know that eczema isn’t really a skin condition, it’s a gut problem and so we found a Dr (thanks to a good friend of ours) who specialises in this (funnily enough he also specialises in thyroid issues; so I’ll have to save up to go and see him myself too!) and he’s asked us to go on an elimination diet for two weeks and then we start introducing a new food/group every couple of days to see what might flare her eczema up again. This will tell us what she’s intolerant to.

This morning we had a melt down over breakfast. Scrambled eggs were served which would usually be eaten with no problem or fuss, but this morning she just wanted weet-bix or peanut butter and honey toast; because she knows she can’t have it (which is why we have never had ‘bad/junk/sometimes’ food labels in our home; food is food and it’s all on offer, but mummy and daddy choose what to offer and she chooses what to eat from what’s on offer and how much of it. 

A few days ago I reached out to my lovely friend Kristy @southerninlaw  who is an absolute recipe developing QUEEN! especially when it comes to food intolerances or allergies. I knew she’d have something for me. I wanted a bliss ball type recipe, using raspberries, dates, coconut, we can use nuts; just not peanuts, and no oats. Straight away she had a recipe for me and suggested we sub out the protein powder with almond meal and blueberries can easily be swapped for the raspberries.

DBzguKCgULw.content:
Unpopular opinion? 

I hope not! 

This morning at school the kids were playing on the monkey bars which are a decent height; at least 2m high. And this little boy who would be either 6 or 7, fell. He fell from that height, flat onto his back; so hard that it stunned and winded him. I went straight over to him to see if he was ok, by the time I made it to him he was already moving which made me a bit nervous, so I encouraged him to just sit back down for a minute to catch his breath which he did. DKioPoUz_uS.content:
Breastfeeding twin toddlers!

We are 2 years, 1 month, 2 weeks and 4 days into our breastfeeding journey. But when will you stop? Seems to be the question society is obsessed with. When they are ready. I fought hard, advocated hard from the very first day the were born and the paediatricians mentioned ‘topping up with formula’ yet they knew I wanted to breastfeed. Mums of twins, triplets and more have to fight extra hard if they want to breastfeed their babies. Because health care professionals; be that paediatricians, GPs, physios, naturopaths,chiropractors, dentists; have little to know knowledge of breastmilk and breastfeeding unless they go out and seek it for themselves (enter @amberley_harris_ 👏🏼)

The amount of terrible and incorrect advice I’ve gotten from well meaning but ill educated HCPs is astounding, and the one that sticks out the most is the paediatrician we were assigned at around 6 months because my twins were not gaining weight as fast as ‘they’ would like. 

Let me tell you, the advice I received from him not only was incorrect, but if I was a mother for the first time or a mother who wasn’t educated on breastfeeding; it literally would have been the beginning of the end of our journey. And it’s crazy because he genuinely believed that what he was saying was true;
“It’s not normal for 6 month olds to feed so often (every 2-3 hours)” WRONG, VERY WRONG!!!

“We see this a lot, it’s hard for your body to make enough milk for TWO babies, you must have low supply” WRONG! If your body can grow and birth two babies and if you have the right knowledge and support, you can absolutely produce enough milk for two (or three or four) babies. Whether you want to or not, is your personal decision, but this was mine. 

“Do you feel full before a feed and empty afterwards” THIS right here was a dead giveaway that he had no clue what he was talking about. At 6 months, your milk production has well and truly regulated and you wouldn’t feel full or empty after every feed ; a soft breast is a healthy breast. 

Follow those I’ve tagged in this reel for GREAT advice and content on breastfeeding!

Just day 2 of school holidays so I wrote a little poem to remind me that yes, parenting small children is fun 🤪

Crumbs in the Carpet

There are dirty handprints all over my walls, and mirrors which look especially bad.  There are crumbs all through the carpet, and bits of dried playdough which drive me mad!  There are clothes all over the floor— an eternal wait to be put back in their place.
Toys scattered all through the house and  more books on the floor than in the bookcase.  There are stains all through the mattresses, and stains all through the sofa.
My makeup’s been taken away to use on the dolls, though hopefully, it can’t go too far.  When I walk in the bathroom, there’s always a puddle of water on the floor.
And when I actually need to go, it seems no one can respect a closed door!  Dishes are piled up in the kitchen, and my condiments have been broken into again.
There’s half-eaten fruit and half-drunk juices lying around—when will the chaos end?  The goal of a clean house just seems like an impossible reality for me,
But does a clean house really mean much, if it’s only achievable when I’m child-free?  The mess and the chaos are signs of little people with imaginations who have fun.
They are signs of a day well-lived, when it’s all said and done.  I can’t expect my home to be spick and span, with no signs of life or living.
I remind myself that I’m blessed by my little people. Tomorrow, I’ll be more forgiving.

DTQoLg1Dz1Y.content:
I want to be very clear:
I still hate that pancreatic cancer is classified as “rare.”

When tens of thousands of families are impacted every single year—and that number continues to rise—it does not feel rare to us.
Last year alone, projections estimated 60,000+ new diagnoses. And we already know that number isn’t going down anytime soon.
So this reel isn’t me walking back my frustration.
It’s me adding context.
Pancreatic cancer is labeled “rare” not because researchers or physicians are dismissive—they aren’t. Many of them are fighting relentlessly for better outcomes for our families.

The classification exists because: • Precancerous pancreatic cells don’t always develop into pancreatic cancer
• Researchers can only screen a very limited population, primarily those with known genetic or hereditary risk factors
• There isn’t enough funding to screen the broader population—especially those with no warning signs at all

That means countless people develop pancreatic cancer without being detectable early. And that’s exactly the problem researchers are trying to solve.
This is why they’re working toward: • Earlier detection
• Pancreatic-specific screening tools
• Preventative measures—similar to what exists for breast, colon, and prostate cancer

So yes—“rare” may be the technical classification.
But in living rooms, hospital rooms, and hospice rooms, pancreatic cancer is far too common.
And that tension?

That’s where advocacy lives.
If you’re navigating this journey as a caregiver or family member, visit our website for education, resources, and support created with you in mind. You don’t have to figure this out alone.

💜 Progress is happening. And we will keep pushing.

DTvhvTVD4va.content:
Pancreatic cancer is often detected late — not because families aren’t paying attention, but because early detection tools are limited.

This is why radiomics matters.
I learned about this work during a webinar hosted by the Lustgarten Foundation, where I heard directly from the experts leading this research — Dr. Elliot Fishman and Dr. Laura Wood.

Dr. Fishman is advancing radiomics, an approach that combines AI with medical imaging to identify cancer risks that traditional scans can miss. Tumors leave behind patterns — and this technology helps detect those warning signs earlier.

Dr. Wood spoke to the realities of surveillance today — how it’s largely limited to those with hereditary risk or known genetic mutations, even though 90% of pancreatic cancers are sporadic.
This is what caregivers need to know: Research is moving.

Physicians and researchers are fighting.
And the future does not have to look like the past.
We still have work to do — but progress is real, and hope is grounded in action.

DUJfwikj3YD.content:
Myth: Clinical trials and treatments are for everyone.

Truth: They’re not — and that doesn’t mean something is wrong with your loved one.

Cancer treatment is highly individualized. What’s available depends on several factors, including: • the specific diagnosis and stage
• tumor type and location
• genetic and molecular findings
• overall health and prior treatments

Oncological teams aren’t excluding people — they’re matching patients to what’s safest, most effective, and most appropriate for their specific case.
This is why two people can have the “same cancer” and very different treatment paths.

It’s not about fairness.
It’s about precision.
And as a caregiver, understanding this helps you ask better questions, advocate with clarity, and release unnecessary guilt when a treatment option isn’t available.

Knowledge doesn’t remove the fear — but it does reduce the confusion.

This is part of what we do at Baylor Strong: helping caregivers understand the why so you’re not left feeling lost in the process.

You can’t control how your loved one responds to treatment.
You can’t control the outcome.
You can’t control how all of this unfolds.

We didn’t meet his oncologist.
We didn’t fully understand what was happening.
And by the time he opened up… we had already lost time.

That put us at a deficit.

and still getting sent in circles trying to find answers.
Different experiences. Same result.

Too much to carry.

That’s where clarity matters.
Because while there’s a lot you can’t control…
there are things you can.

My role is to help you focus there.
To help you understand your options and your next steps—without the overwhelm.

Like… genuinely pissed.

Because I couldn’t understand it.

Why does it feel like my family just keeps getting hit back to back?

And then on top of that… my dad?
My dad??

Out of all people?

He was young. Early 60s. Still living life. Still being him.
And I’m sitting there thinking—out of ALL the cancers… why this one?
The one with no real cure? The one I already watched take my aunt when I was younger?

My mind was everywhere.
“He’s gonna die.”
“He’s not gonna make it.”
“This isn’t fair.”

I was spiraling and angry at the same time.

It’s raw.
It’s heavy.
It’s a whole lot of “why them?” and “why us?”

You’re not the only one wondering if postpartum planning will actually work for you, and these questions come up all the time. ✨

I’m answering the most common concerns I hear from new and growing families:

💬 “Is this only for first-time mums?”
It's for anyone expecting a baby! Often second-time mums find postpartum planning even more worthwhile...because you already know how hard it can be, and this time you want to do it differently. You'll naturally focus more on some modules than others, and that's completely fine.

💬 “Isn't this what my midwife is for?”
Your midwife provides clinical care. Postpartum planning encompasses a broader, holistic approach, and covers a longer timeframe: the emotional landscape, your relationships, the home, sleep, what it actually feels like to step into motherhood, and more.

💬 "What if my situation, or my birth preferences, change?"
A comprehensive postpartum plan gives you a strong foundation to adapt from, so when things shift, the whole thing doesn't topple over. You'll be far better equipped to handle the unexpected if you've already thought through your needs.

💬 "Is it really all that complicated?"
Many mothers assume they should be able to figure this out on their own. And yet most mothers look back and say, "I wish I had known." Birthing and caring for a baby is one of the hardest things a human can do. It makes sense to prepare for it.

Postpartum shouldn’t feel like guesswork. It should feel supported, spacious, and steady with someone in your corner who actually understands the mental load, the emotions, and the day-to-day reality you’re stepping into.

DWN1KSRjOyN.content:
You learnt so much the first time around, but there are new challenges with baby #2 as well.

Here are 4 things that challenge my mums when they have their second baby:

✨ 𝒀𝒐𝒖𝒓 𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒊𝒔 𝒔𝒖𝒅𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒍𝒚 𝒔𝒑𝒍𝒊𝒕.
Both children need you...often at the exact same time. Learning how to meet everyone’s needs (including your own) can take time.

✨ 𝒀𝒐𝒖𝒓 𝒐𝒍𝒅𝒆𝒓 𝒄𝒉𝒊𝒍𝒅 𝒊𝒔 𝒂𝒅𝒋𝒖𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒕𝒐𝒐.
Even the most chill big sibling will go through an emotional upheaval. Sometimes their behaviour signals a need for increased reassurance, connection, and patience. It can feel intense when you're running on little sleep, and you're craving a quiet newborn bubble.

✨ 𝑹𝒆𝒔𝒕 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒃𝒆 𝒉𝒂𝒓𝒅𝒆𝒓 𝒕𝒐 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒃𝒚.
With your first baby, you could rest when they slept. With baby #2, there’s usually a toddler needing attention or to be supported to sleep as well.

✨ 𝑰𝒕 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒇𝒆𝒆𝒍 𝒍𝒊𝒌𝒆 𝒚𝒐𝒖'𝒓𝒆 𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒔𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒐𝒖𝒕.
Some mothers miss their alone time with their first child, or the snuggles through the night. While other mums crave more time in the newborn bubble, and can even resent their older child for making it more challenging. It's normal, but it's also still really hard.

You're welcoming your second child to the family, and you know it will be different this time - but how, exactly?

Here are 4  challenges you might experience during postpartum with your second baby:

✨ 𝒀𝒐𝒖𝒓 𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒊𝒔 𝒔𝒖𝒅𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒍𝒚 𝒔𝒑𝒍𝒊𝒕.
Both children need you...often at the exact same time. Learning how to meet everyone’s needs (including your own) can take time.

✨ 𝒀𝒐𝒖𝒓 𝒐𝒍𝒅𝒆𝒓 𝒄𝒉𝒊𝒍𝒅 𝒊𝒔 𝒂𝒅𝒋𝒖𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒕𝒐𝒐.
Even the most chill big sibling will go through an emotional upheaval. Sometimes their behaviour signals a need for increased reassurance, connection, and patience. It can feel intense when you're running on little sleep, and you're craving a quiet newborn bubble.

✨ 𝑹𝒆𝒔𝒕 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒃𝒆 𝒉𝒂𝒓𝒅𝒆𝒓 𝒕𝒐 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒆 𝒃𝒚.
With your first baby, you could rest when they slept. With the second, there’s usually a toddler needing one-on-one time, or to be supported to sleep as well. 

✨ 𝑰𝒕 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒇𝒆𝒆𝒍 𝒍𝒊𝒌𝒆 𝒚𝒐𝒖'𝒓𝒆 𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒔𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒐𝒖𝒕.
Some mothers miss their alone time with their first child, or the snuggles through the night. While other mums crave more time in the newborn bubble, and can even resent their older child for making it more challenging. It's normal, but it's also still really hard.

This is why postpartum support is so valuable the second time around.🥰

An extra set of hands to hold, soothe, play and distract has been a game-changer for my fourth-trimester clients. ✨❤

DWvFy7wAe5K.content:
“The newborn will sleep a lot.”🤍

We've all heard it. I've even SAID it. But the reality is a little more nuanced and this nuance often fails to translate when speaking to those yet to have their baby.

Newborn sleep isn’t long, predictable rest. You might get lucky and have a few days of long sleeps straight after birth. Maybe the lactation consultant will even encourage you to wake your baby every four hours for a breastfeed! (that'll hurt!)

But unfortunately these few days, and the myths we're told, tend to lure new parents into a false sense of security. 

Your newborn will likely sleep in short cycles for the whole fourth trimester, with frequent waking, and days that blur into nights.🌙

The issue is when your expectations don’t match that reality, postpartum can feel more overwhelming. It can seem like you're doing something wrong, or that you're not coping like you thought you would. 

But you are not causing your newborn to wake frequently. Most of the time, this is just normal newborn behaviour.

And you're not falling short, just because you're exhausted and overwhelmed. 🫶This is a reasonable reaction to a very extreme set of circumstances for your body and your mind.

✨ Understanding all this helps you prepare differently.
✨ It gives you permission to arrange support in advance.
✨ It softens the pressure you place on yourself.

📩Message me if you're looking for more guidance on this topic. I'd love to help.

DXvds4DDsyO.content:
There’s a prevalent assumption that postpartum is just… rough.
Like you’re *meant* to be exhausted, overwhelmed, and barely keeping it together.

And yes, I'm definitely a BIG fan of realistic expectations - the sleep deprivation can be, well, torture. And nothing can quite prepare you for the labour intensity of caring for newborns.

But that's not what makes it feel so rough...not really.

What really makes it feel horrible is not the baby stuff. 
✦ It's the lack of support, 
✦ The “you’ll be right” mentality,
✦ The absence of quality preparation for what happens after birth.

The combo of these factors leads to new parents feeling blindsided, depressed, anxious, and burnt out.

But the good news is: while we may not be able to control our newborn's sleep patterns, or how many times they need a feed or a nappy change...

we CAN control:
✦ how wide we cast our village and support net,
✦ how much we teach and learn about postpartum and motherhood, 
✦ and we can, in a way, control our mindset. 

With the right support around you, postpartum can feel quite lovely. If you’re expecting (or planning ahead), now’s the time to think about your postpartum planning and support.

DYJiT-4Gs1O.content:
Sometimes our significant others or family members miss the mark. It’s so common, and I’ve been there. It feels so hurtful to be let down on an important day that is supposed to be all about YOU!!

What’s worse, is so many mothers internalise this hurt as a personal failure. Like our expectations were too high, we didn’t communicate what we wanted clearly enough, or even that we made a poor selection 10 years ago when we chose to marry someone who obviously doesn’t know how to plan a special occasion!! 😅

But I’m here to tell you, that your expectations for being loved, honoured, and pampered are not ‘too high’. Unless you were expecting a private jet ride to Paris and you’re NOT Kim Kardashian, then chances are your desires were pretty reasonable.

Motherhood truly is the hardest job in the world. We’re doing motherhood without enough support, in a time when productivity is rewarded and care-work is devalued. And we have every right to be annoyed about that, and to demand better. 

If your loved ones didn’t help you feel seen this Mother’s Day, please know that I SEE YOU. I see you holding everything together with one arm while a baby is in your other. I see your toddler yanking your top down to breastfeed while you’re on a yoga mat in Downward Dog, desperately trying to strengthen your poor tired body. I see you yelling at the kids and feeling the shame and guilt that you didn’t use Gentle Parenting! I see you feeling alone in this.

And even though we shouldn’t have to do this alone, without reward, without enough validation and respect from even our life partner sometimes…I just want to remind you that you are resilient. It’s in your DNA, your neural wiring, your new Mother identity - you have more resilience in your pinky finger than some people (*cough* men *cough*) have in their whole body. You will survive this, like you always do. Because Mums rule.

From one Mum to another, Happy Mothers Day you absolute QUEEN!👑💕

XO, Jas

DYDF1OXDXdv.content:
Did you feel seriously changed postpartum? Like you were transformed somehow and would never be the same again? 

You're not imagining it, mama. I am almost 6 months pregnant as I write these words and I feel myself shifting again, but I'm  it fighting it any more.

DYHLtRVDNjU.accessibility_caption:
Advice about the safety of drinking alcohol whilst breastfeeding varies widely depending upon the source. You may find yourself bombarded with conflicting information about whether a glass of bubbles or a few beers are safe for you to consume as a breastfeeding mother. You might have heard from a friend that it is totally fine to breastfeed after a few drinks, but you have almost certainly also heard that you need to pump and dump your milk after consuming alcohol. So what are the facts? Is it safe to have a glass of wine or two whilst breastfeeding? If so, how much? Does alcohol get into your milk supply - and is there ever a need to pump and dump after a drink? 



The NHS, advises nursing and pumping mothers that, "An occasional drink is unlikely to harm your baby, especially if you wait at least 2 hours after having a drink before feeding...Regularly drinking above the recommended limits can be harmful for you and your baby." (1) The American Academy of Pediatrics has similar advice, adding that alcohol can impact milk production (2). These recommendations are based upon the fact that it takes around two hours after the consumption of alcohol for your blood alcohol levels to return to zero as a breastfeeding mother. If you choose to consume alcohol whilst breastfeeding, it is worth knowing that your blood alcohol levels peak after around 30-60 minutes, or 60 - 90 minutes if consumed with food (4). So if you want to minimise the amount of alcohol passed onto your nursling through your milk, it would be best to nurse them either as you are drinking an alcoholic beverage or an several hours after doing so.  



Does Alcohol Pass into my Milk?



In short, the answer is yes - in tiny quantities. For example, if a 75kg woman were to consume six glasses of wine in quick succession, my blood alcohol level would peak at 0.17% (5). If I were to then breastfeed my baby, 5-6% of that alcohol would be passed on through my milk. This would mean that it would contain 0.01% alcohol. To put that into context, orange juice has an ABV measure of 0.07% (6). It is also with knowing that alcohol passes into and out of your milk freely as your body metabolizes it. Therefore, there is no need to pump and dump simply because you have had a glass of bubbles at a party. If you were to consume large amounts of alcohol, it would be advisable to wait at least a few hours until your blood alcohol levels were lower before nursing or pumping for your baby. 



Whilst the amount of alcohol in your breast milk may be your primary concern as a nursing or pumping mama, it should not be the only consideration. For instance, if you choose to consume alcohol whilst breastfeeding, it is important to remember that you cannot safely bedshare with your baby after doing so (7). Additionally, it is likely that after multiple alcoholic drinks, you will feel tipsy or even drunk. In this case, your ability to care for your baby could be compromised because of the risks of falling and so on. Whilst it may well be safe for you to nurse your little one after a drink, caring for them safely could be the greater challenge. With this in mind, planning for another loving caregiver to look after your child after a particularly merry night out is advisable.
